Theorem (Euler Maclaurin Formula Expansion):
Given positive integers \(n\) and \(N\), the sum of the reciprocals of the squares of the first \(n\) natural numbers is approximated by \(\pi^2/6 - 1/n + 1/(2n^2)\) minus a sum involving Bernoulli numbers and a remainder term. This theorem connects discrete summation with integral calculus, providing an asymptotic expansion for the sum of reciprocals of squares, which is useful in various mathematical analyses.

lemma sum_inverse_squares_expansion:
  assumes n: "n > 0" and N: "N > 0"
  shows "(∑k=1..n. 1 / real k ^ 2) = 
            pi ^ 2 / 6 - 1 / real n + 1 / (2 * real n ^ 2) -
                     (∑i=1..N. bernoulli (2*i) / n ^ (2*i+1)) - 
                    EM_remainder (2*N+1) (λx. -fact (2*N+2) / x ^ (2*N+3)) (int n)"
proof -
  have 3: "3 = Suc (Suc (Suc 0))" by (simp add: eval_nat_numeral)
  define fs where "fs = (λk x. (-1) ^ k * fact (Suc k) / x ^ (k+2) :: real)"    
  interpret euler_maclaurin_nat' "λx. -1/x" "λx. 1/x^2" fs 1 N "pi^2/6" "{}"
  proof
    fix k x assume "k ≤ 2*N" "x ∈ {real 1..} - {}"
    thus "(fs k has_vector_derivative fs (Suc k) x) (at x)"
      by (cases "k = 0")
         (auto intro!: derivative_eq_intros 
               simp: fs_def has_real_derivative_iff_has_vector_derivative [symmetric] 
                     field_simps power_diff)
  next
    from inverse_squares_sums
      have "(λn. ∑k<n. 1 / real (Suc k) ^ 2) ⇢ pi⇧2 / 6" by (simp add: sums_def)
    also have "(λn. ∑k<n. 1 / real (Suc k) ^ 2) = (λn. ∑k=1..n. 1 / real k ^ 2)"
      by (intro ext sum.reindex_bij_witness[of _ "λn. n - 1" Suc]) auto
    finally have "(λb. (∑k = 1..b. 1 / real k^2) + 1 / real b -
                 (∑i<2*N+1. bernoulli' (Suc i) * (- 1) ^ i / (real b ^ (i+2))))
            ⇢ (pi^2/6 + 0 - (∑i<2*N+1. 0))"
      by (intro tendsto_diff tendsto_add real_tendsto_divide_at_top[OF tendsto_const] 
            filterlim_tendsto_pos_mult_at_top[OF tendsto_const] filterlim_pow_at_top
            filterlim_real_sequentially tendsto_sum) auto
    thus "(λb. (∑k = 1..b. 1 / real k^2) - (- 1 / real b) - 
            (∑i<2*N+1. (bernoulli' (Suc i) / fact (Suc i)) *⇩R fs i (real b))) ⇢ pi^2/6"
      by (simp add: harm_def field_simps fs_def del: power_Suc of_nat_Suc)
  qed (insert n N, auto intro!: continuous_intros derivative_eq_intros
         simp: fs_def has_real_derivative_iff_has_vector_derivative [symmetric] power2_eq_square)

  have "(∑k=1..n. 1 / real k ^ 2) = - 1 / real n + pi^2/6 + (1/2) *⇩R (1 / real n^2) +
               (∑i=1..N. (bernoulli (2*i) / fact (2*i)) *⇩R fs (2*i-1) (real n)) -
               EM_remainder (2*N+1) (fs (2*N+1)) (int n)" using n N
    using n by (intro euler_maclaurin_strong_nat') simp_all
  also have "(∑i=1..N. (bernoulli (2*i) / fact (2*i)) *⇩R (fs (2*i-1) (real n))) =
               (∑i=1..N. -(bernoulli (2*i) / (real n ^ (2*i+1))))"
    by (intro sum.cong refl) 
       (simp_all add: fs_def divide_simps fact_reduce del: of_nat_Suc power_Suc)
  also have "… = -(∑i=1..N. bernoulli (2*i) / real n ^ (2*i+1))"
    by (simp add: sum_negf)
  finally show ?thesis unfolding fs_def by (simp add: fs_def 3)
qed

Theorem (Leibniz Formula for π):
The value of π/4 is equal to the alternating sum of the reciprocals of the odd numbers multiplied by 2, expressed as \(\frac{\pi}{4} = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^k}{1 + 2k}\).

theorem pi_series: "pi/4 = (∑k. (-1)^k * 1 / real (k * 2 + 1))"
  (is "_ = ?SUM")
proof -
  have "pi/4 = arctan 1"
    using arctan_one by auto
  also have "… = ?SUM"
    using arctan_series[of 1] by auto
  finally show ?thesis by auto
qed

The sum of the squares of the first n natural numbers is given by the formula \(\frac{1}{6}n(n+1)(2n+1)\). This is derived using Bernoulli numbers and properties of sums of powers.

theorem sum_of_squares: "real (∑k≤n::nat. k ^ 2) = real (2 * n ^ 3 + 3 * n ^ 2 + n) / 6"
  unfolding of_nat_sum of_nat_power sum_of_powers
  by (simp add: bernoulli_unroll_all field_simps power2_eq_square power_numeral_reduce)

Theorem (Möbius Function over Square Sums):
The Möbius function, denoted by μ(n), when applied to the sum of its values over the squares of natural numbers, yields a constant value, specifically the ratio of 6 to the square of π (approximately 0.36602540378443865).

lemma moebius_over_square_sums: "(λn. moebius_mu n / n⇧2) sums (6 / pi⇧2)"
proof -
  have "1 = eval_fds (1 :: real fds) 2" by simp
  also have "(1 :: real fds) = fds_zeta * fds moebius_mu" 
    by (rule fds_zeta_times_moebius_mu [symmetric])
  also have "eval_fds … 2 = eval_fds fds_zeta 2 * eval_fds (fds moebius_mu) 2"
    by (intro eval_fds_mult fds_abs_converges_moebius_mu_real) simp_all
  also have "… = pi ^ 2 / 6 * (∑n. moebius_mu n / (real n)⇧2)"
    using inverse_squares_sums' by (simp add: eval_fds_at_numeral suminf_fds_zeta_aux sums_iff)
  finally have "(∑n. moebius_mu n / (real n)⇧2) = 6 / pi ^ 2" by (simp add: field_simps)
  with summable_moebius_over_square show ?thesis by (simp add: sums_iff)
qed

Corollary (Hurwitz Zeta Function at 6):
The Hurwitz zeta function evaluated at 6, denoted as \(\zeta(6)\), is equal to \(\frac{\pi^6}{945}\).

corollary zeta_6: "zeta 6 = pi ^ 6 / 945"
  by (simp add: zeta_even_numeral fact_num_eq_if)

Theorem (Euler Maclaurin Formula for Summations):
Given a natural number \(N\), the sum of the reciprocals of the squares of the first \(N\) natural numbers, when adjusted by a specific correction term \(T\), is bounded above by a term that decreases rapidly as \(N\) increases. Specifically, the difference between the sum and the correction term \(T\) is of the order \(O(1/N^{2+2N})\), where \(O\) denotes the big-O notation indicating the upper bound of the growth rate.

lemma sum_inverse_squares_expansion_bigo:
  fixes N :: nat
  defines "T ≡ λn. pi ^ 2 / 6 - 1 / n + 1 / (2*n ^ 2) -
                     (∑i=1..N. bernoulli (2*i) / (n ^ (2*i+1)))"
  defines "S ≡ (λn. bernoulli (2*(Suc N)) / (real n ^ (2*N+3)))"
  shows "(λn. (∑i=1..n. 1 / real i ^ 2) - T n) ∈ O(λn. 1 / real n ^ (2 * N + 3))"
proof -
  have 3: "3 = Suc (Suc (Suc 0))" by simp

Theorem (Jacobi's Square Theorem for Squares):
Given a natural number \(n\), the number of ways to express \(n\) as a sum of two squares, denoted by \(r(n)\), is equal to the count of divisors of \(n\) that are squares, i.e., \(r(n) = \text{divisors}(n) \cap \text{squares}\).

This theorem relates the representation of natural numbers as sums of two squares to the divisors of those numbers that are perfect squares. The lemma provided suggests a method to compute this count using a function that identifies square divisors.

lemma sos_decomps_1:

Theorem (Square Part of a Natural Number):
Given a natural number \(n\), the square part of \(n\) is the product of its prime factors raised to the power of half their count. Specifically, if \(n\) is not zero, it can be expressed as \(n = \prod_{p \in \text{set}(n)} p^{(\text{count}(p, n)/2)}\), where \(\text{count}(p, n)\) denotes the number of times \(p\) divides \(n\).

This theorem is related to the properties of continued fractions, particularly in distinguishing between rational and irrational numbers through their periodic or non-periodic continued fraction expansions. Rational numbers have finite continued fraction expansions, while irrational numbers, especially quadratic irrationals, have periodic expansions. The formalization of continued fractions in this context helps in understanding the underlying structure of real numbers and their representations.

lemma square_part_nat_code [code_unfold]:
  "square_part (n :: nat) = (if n = 0 then 0
     else let ps = prime_factorization n in  (∏p∈set_mset ps. p ^ (count ps p div 2)))"
  using square_squarefree_part_nat_code[of n]
  by (simp add: square_squarefree_part_nat_def Let_def split: if_splits)

Theorem (Sum of Inverse Squares):
The sum of the inverses of the squares of the first \(n\) natural numbers is given by the formula \(\sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{1}{i^2} = \frac{\pi^2}{6}\).

theorem inverse_squares_sums: "(λn. 1 / (n + 1)⇧2) sums (pi⇧2 / 6)"
proof -
  define P where "P x n = (∏k=1..n. 1 - x^2 / of_nat k^2)" for x :: real and n
  define K where "K = (∑n. inverse (real_of_nat (Suc n))^2)"
  define f where [abs_def]: "f x = (∑n. P x n / of_nat (Suc n)^2)" for x
  define g where [abs_def]: "g x = (1 - sin (pi * x) / (pi * x))" for x

  have sums: "(λn. P x n / of_nat (Suc n)^2) sums (if x = 0 then K else g x / x^2)" for x
  proof (cases "x = 0")
    assume x: "x = 0"
    have "summable (λn. inverse ((real_of_nat (Suc n))⇧2))"
      using inverse_power_summable[of 2] by (subst summable_Suc_iff) simp
    thus ?thesis by (simp add: x g_def P_def K_def inverse_eq_divide power_divide summable_sums)
  next
    assume x: "x ≠ 0"
    have "(λn. P x n - P x (Suc n)) sums (P x 0 - sin (pi * x) / (pi * x))"
      unfolding P_def using x by (intro telescope_sums' sin_product_formula_real')
    also have "(λn. P x n - P x (Suc n)) = (λn. (x^2 / of_nat (Suc n)^2) * P x n)"
      unfolding P_def by (simp add: prod.nat_ivl_Suc' algebra_simps)
    also have "P x 0 = 1" by (simp add: P_def)
    finally have "(λn. x⇧2 / (of_nat (Suc n))⇧2 * P x n) sums (1 - sin (pi * x) / (pi * x))" .
    from sums_divide[OF this, of "x^2"] x show ?thesis unfolding g_def by simp
  qed

  have "continuous_on (ball 0 1) f"
  proof (rule uniform_limit_theorem; (intro always_eventually allI)?)
    show "uniform_limit (ball 0 1) (λn x. ∑k<n. P x k / of_nat (Suc k)^2) f sequentially"
    proof (unfold f_def, rule Weierstrass_m_test)
      fix n :: nat and x :: real assume x: "x ∈ ball 0 1"
      {
        fix k :: nat assume k: "k ≥ 1"
        from x have "x^2 < 1" by (auto simp: abs_square_less_1)
        also from k have "… ≤ of_nat k^2" by simp
        finally have "(1 - x^2 / of_nat k^2) ∈ {0..1}" using k
          by (simp_all add: field_simps del: of_nat_Suc)
      }
      hence "(∏k=1..n. abs (1 - x^2 / of_nat k^2)) ≤ (∏k=1..n. 1)" by (intro prod_mono) simp
      thus "norm (P x n / (of_nat (Suc n)^2)) ≤ 1 / of_nat (Suc n)^2"
        unfolding P_def by (simp add: field_simps abs_prod del: of_nat_Suc)
    qed (subst summable_Suc_iff, insert inverse_power_summable[of 2], simp add: inverse_eq_divide)
  qed (auto simp: P_def intro!: continuous_intros)
  hence "isCont f 0" by (subst (asm) continuous_on_eq_continuous_at) simp_all
  hence "(f ─ 0 → f 0)" by (simp add: isCont_def)
  also have "f 0 = K" unfolding f_def P_def K_def by (simp add: inverse_eq_divide power_divide)
  finally have "f ─ 0 → K" .

  moreover have "f ─ 0 → pi^2 / 6"
  proof (rule Lim_transform_eventually)
    define f' where [abs_def]: "f' x = (∑n. - sin_coeff (n+3) * pi ^ (n+2) * x^n)" for x
    have "eventually (λx. x ≠ (0::real)) (at 0)"
      by (auto simp add: eventually_at intro!: exI[of _ 1])
    thus "eventually (λx. f' x = f x) (at 0)"
    proof eventually_elim
      fix x :: real assume x: "x ≠ 0"
      have "sin_coeff 1 = (1 :: real)" "sin_coeff 2 = (0::real)" by (simp_all add: sin_coeff_def)
      with sums_split_initial_segment[OF sums_minus[OF sin_converges], of 3 "pi*x"]
      have "(λn. - (sin_coeff (n+3) * (pi*x)^(n+3))) sums (pi * x - sin (pi*x))"
        by (simp add: eval_nat_numeral)
      from sums_divide[OF this, of "x^3 * pi"] x
        have "(λn. - (sin_coeff (n+3) * pi^(n+2) * x^n)) sums ((1 - sin (pi*x) / (pi*x)) / x^2)"
        by (simp add: field_split_simps eval_nat_numeral)
      with x have "(λn. - (sin_coeff (n+3) * pi^(n+2) * x^n)) sums (g x / x^2)"
        by (simp add: g_def)
      hence "f' x = g x / x^2" by (simp add: sums_iff f'_def)
      also have "… = f x" using sums[of x] x by (simp add: sums_iff g_def f_def)
      finally show "f' x = f x" .
    qed

    have "isCont f' 0" unfolding f'_def
    proof (intro isCont_powser_converges_everywhere)
      fix x :: real show "summable (λn. -sin_coeff (n+3) * pi^(n+2) * x^n)"
      proof (cases "x = 0")
        assume x: "x ≠ 0"
        from summable_divide[OF sums_summable[OF sums_split_initial_segment[OF
               sin_converges[of "pi*x"]], of 3], of "-pi*x^3"] x
          show ?thesis by (simp add: field_split_simps eval_nat_numeral)
      qed (simp only: summable_0_powser)
    qed
    hence "f' ─ 0 → f' 0" by (simp add: isCont_def)
    also have "f' 0 = pi * pi / fact 3" unfolding f'_def
      by (subst powser_zero) (simp add: sin_coeff_def)
    finally show "f' ─ 0 → pi^2 / 6" by (simp add: eval_nat_numeral)
  qed

  ultimately have "K = pi^2 / 6" by (rule LIM_unique)
  moreover from inverse_power_summable[of 2]
    have "summable (λn. (inverse (real_of_nat (Suc n)))⇧2)"
    by (subst summable_Suc_iff) (simp add: power_inverse)
  ultimately show ?thesis unfolding K_def
    by (auto simp add: sums_iff power_divide inverse_eq_divide)
qed

Theorem (Jacobi's Square Theorem for Squares Function):
Given a natural number \(n\), the number of ways to express \(n\) as a sum of two squares, denoted by \(r(n)\), is equal to the count of divisors of \(n\) that are congruent to 1 modulo 4, after normalization. Mathematically, \(r(n) = \text{count of divisors of } n \text{ congruent to } 1 \mod 4\), where the count is normalized.

lemma gauss_ints_with_norm'_2_power: "gauss_ints_with_norm' (2 ^ n) = {normalize ((1 + 𝗂⇩ℤ) ^ n)}"
proof -
  define p where "p = 1 + 𝗂⇩ℤ"
  have p: "p ≠ 0" "gauss_int_norm p = 2" "prime p"
    by (auto simp: p_def gauss_int_eq_iff gauss_int_norm_def prime_one_plus_i_gauss_int)
  show ?thesis
  proof (intro equalityI subsetI; (elim singletonE; hypsubst)?)
    show "normalize ((1 + 𝗂⇩ℤ) ^ n) ∈ gauss_ints_with_norm' (2 ^ n)"
      unfolding p_def [symmetric]
      using p by (auto simp: gauss_ints_with_norm'_def gauss_int_norm_power)
  next
    fix z assume "z ∈ gauss_ints_with_norm' (2 ^ n)"
    hence z: "gauss_int_norm z = 2 ^ n" "normalize z = z"
      by (auto simp: gauss_ints_with_norm'_def)
    from z have "2 ^ n = z * gauss_cnj z"
      by (simp add: self_mult_gauss_cnj)
    also have "2 = -𝗂⇩ℤ * p ^ 2"
      by (auto simp: p_def power2_eq_square algebra_simps)
    also have "… ^ n = (-𝗂⇩ℤ) ^ n * p ^ (2 * n)"
      by (simp add: algebra_simps power_minus' flip: power_mult)
    finally have "z dvd (-𝗂⇩ℤ) ^ n * p ^ (2 * n)"
      by auto
    moreover have "is_unit ((-𝗂⇩ℤ) ^ n)"
      by auto
    ultimately have "z dvd p ^ (2 * n)"
      using dvd_mult_unit_iff' by blast
    with ‹prime p› obtain i where i: "i ≤ 2 * n" "z = normalize (p ^ i)"
      using divides_primepow_weak[of p z "2*n"] z by auto
    with z p have "i = n"
      by (simp add: gauss_int_norm_power)
    with i show "z ∈ {normalize ((1 + gauss_i) ^ n)}"
      by (simp add: p_def)
  qed
qed

Theorem (Euler Maclaurin Formula Expansion):
Given positive integers \(n\) and \(N\), the sum of the reciprocals of the squares of the first \(n\) natural numbers is approximated by \(\pi^2/6 - 1/n + 1/(2n^2)\) minus a sum involving Bernoulli numbers and a remainder term. This theorem connects discrete summation with integral calculus, providing an asymptotic expansion for the sum of reciprocals of squares, which is useful in various mathematical analyses.

lemma sum_inverse_squares_expansion:
  assumes n: "n > 0" and N: "N > 0"
  shows "(∑k=1..n. 1 / real k ^ 2) = 
            pi ^ 2 / 6 - 1 / real n + 1 / (2 * real n ^ 2) -
                     (∑i=1..N. bernoulli (2*i) / n ^ (2*i+1)) - 
                    EM_remainder (2*N+1) (λx. -fact (2*N+2) / x ^ (2*N+3)) (int n)"
proof -
  have 3: "3 = Suc (Suc (Suc 0))" by (simp add: eval_nat_numeral)
  define fs where "fs = (λk x. (-1) ^ k * fact (Suc k) / x ^ (k+2) :: real)"    
  interpret euler_maclaurin_nat' "λx. -1/x" "λx. 1/x^2" fs 1 N "pi^2/6" "{}"
  proof
    fix k x assume "k ≤ 2*N" "x ∈ {real 1..} - {}"
    thus "(fs k has_vector_derivative fs (Suc k) x) (at x)"
      by (cases "k = 0")
         (auto intro!: derivative_eq_intros 
               simp: fs_def has_real_derivative_iff_has_vector_derivative [symmetric] 
                     field_simps power_diff)
  next
    from inverse_squares_sums
      have "(λn. ∑k<n. 1 / real (Suc k) ^ 2) ⇢ pi⇧2 / 6" by (simp add: sums_def)
    also have "(λn. ∑k<n. 1 / real (Suc k) ^ 2) = (λn. ∑k=1..n. 1 / real k ^ 2)"
      by (intro ext sum.reindex_bij_witness[of _ "λn. n - 1" Suc]) auto
    finally have "(λb. (∑k = 1..b. 1 / real k^2) + 1 / real b -
                 (∑i<2*N+1. bernoulli' (Suc i) * (- 1) ^ i / (real b ^ (i+2))))
            ⇢ (pi^2/6 + 0 - (∑i<2*N+1. 0))"
      by (intro tendsto_diff tendsto_add real_tendsto_divide_at_top[OF tendsto_const] 
            filterlim_tendsto_pos_mult_at_top[OF tendsto_const] filterlim_pow_at_top
            filterlim_real_sequentially tendsto_sum) auto
    thus "(λb. (∑k = 1..b. 1 / real k^2) - (- 1 / real b) - 
            (∑i<2*N+1. (bernoulli' (Suc i) / fact (Suc i)) *⇩R fs i (real b))) ⇢ pi^2/6"
      by (simp add: harm_def field_simps fs_def del: power_Suc of_nat_Suc)
  qed (insert n N, auto intro!: continuous_intros derivative_eq_intros
         simp: fs_def has_real_derivative_iff_has_vector_derivative [symmetric] power2_eq_square)

  have "(∑k=1..n. 1 / real k ^ 2) = - 1 / real n + pi^2/6 + (1/2) *⇩R (1 / real n^2) +
               (∑i=1..N. (bernoulli (2*i) / fact (2*i)) *⇩R fs (2*i-1) (real n)) -
               EM_remainder (2*N+1) (fs (2*N+1)) (int n)" using n N
    using n by (intro euler_maclaurin_strong_nat') simp_all
  also have "(∑i=1..N. (bernoulli (2*i) / fact (2*i)) *⇩R (fs (2*i-1) (real n))) =
               (∑i=1..N. -(bernoulli (2*i) / (real n ^ (2*i+1))))"
    by (intro sum.cong refl) 
       (simp_all add: fs_def divide_simps fact_reduce del: of_nat_Suc power_Suc)
  also have "… = -(∑i=1..N. bernoulli (2*i) / real n ^ (2*i+1))"
    by (simp add: sum_negf)
  finally show ?thesis unfolding fs_def by (simp add: fs_def 3)
qed

Theorem (Sum of Squares of the First n Natural Numbers):
For any natural number \(n\), the sum of the squares of the first \(n\) natural numbers is given by \(n\) times the successor of \(n\), plus twice the product of \(n\) and the successor of \(2n\), that is, \(6 \cdot \sum_{i=0}^{n} i^2 = n \cdot Suc(n) + 2 \cdot n \cdot Suc(2n)\).

lemma sum_of_squares: "6 * (∑i=0..n. i * i) = n * Suc n * Suc (2 * n)"
  by (induct n) auto

Theorem (The Core Principle of Area and Difference):
This theorem establishes the relationship between continuous functions over an interval, stating that if a function is integrable on [a, b], then its integral from a to any point c in this range can be calculated by evaluating the difference or sum of values at specific points within the given bounds. This principle serves as a bridge connecting definite integrals and their corresponding antiderivatives for continuous functions over an interval.

top_results.embedding_string:
Theorem (Fundamental Theorem of Calculus for Integrable Functions on an Interval):
Given a real-valued function \( f \) that is continuous and differentiable on the interval \([a, b]\), and integrable over that interval, the definite integral of \( f \) from \( a \) to \( b \) equals the difference between the values of its antiderivative at \( b \) and \( a \), expressed as \(\int_a^b f(x) \, dx = F(b) - F(a)\), where \( F \) is the antiderivative of \( f \).

theorem interval_integral_FTC_integrable:
  fixes f F :: "real ⇒ 'a::euclidean_space" and a b :: ereal
  assumes "a < b"
  assumes F: "⋀x. a < ereal x ⟹ ereal x < b ⟹ (F has_vector_derivative f x) (at x)"
  assumes f: "⋀x. a < ereal x ⟹ ereal x < b ⟹ isCont f x"
  assumes f_integrable: "set_integrable lborel (einterval a b) f"
  assumes A: "((F ∘ real_of_ereal) ⤏ A) (at_right a)"
  assumes B: "((F ∘ real_of_ereal) ⤏ B) (at_left b)"
  shows "(LBINT x=a..b. f x) = B - A"
proof -
  obtain u l where approx:
    "einterval a b = (⋃i. {l i .. u i})"
    "incseq u" "decseq l" "⋀i. l i < u i" "⋀i. a < l i" "⋀i. u i < b"
    "l ⇢ a" "u ⇢ b" 
    by (blast intro: einterval_Icc_approximation[OF ‹a < b›])
  have [simp]: "⋀x i. l i ≤ x ⟹ a < ereal x"
    by (rule order_less_le_trans, rule approx, force)
  have [simp]: "⋀x i. x ≤ u i ⟹ ereal x < b"
    by (rule order_le_less_trans, subst ereal_less_eq(3), assumption, rule approx)
  have FTCi: "⋀i. (LBINT x=l i..u i. f x) = F (u i) - F (l i)"
    using assms approx
    by (auto simp: less_imp_le min_def max_def
             intro!: f continuous_at_imp_continuous_on interval_integral_FTC_finite
             intro: has_vector_derivative_at_within)
  have "(λi. LBINT x=l i..u i. f x) ⇢ B - A"
    unfolding FTCi
  proof (intro tendsto_intros)
    show "(λx. F (l x)) ⇢ A"
      using A approx unfolding tendsto_at_iff_sequentially comp_def
      by (elim allE[of _ "λi. ereal (l i)"], auto)
    show "(λx. F (u x)) ⇢ B"
      using B approx unfolding tendsto_at_iff_sequentially comp_def
      by (elim allE[of _ "λi. ereal (u i)"], auto)
  qed
  moreover have "(λi. LBINT x=l i..u i. f x) ⇢ (LBINT x=a..b. f x)"
    by (rule interval_integral_Icc_approx_integrable [OF ‹a < b› approx f_integrable])
  ultimately show ?thesis
    by (elim LIMSEQ_unique)
qed

Theorem (Integral of a Function over a Closed Interval):
Given two real numbers, \(a\) and \(b\), if \(a \leq b\), then the integral of a function \(f\) over the interval \([a, b]\) is equal to the integral of \(f\) over the set of points from \(a\) to \(b\).

lemma interval_integral_Icc:
  fixes a b :: real
  shows "a ≤ b ⟹ (LBINT x=a..b. f x) = (LBINT x : {a..b}. f x)"
  by (auto intro!: set_integral_discrete_difference[where X="{a, b}"]
           simp add: interval_lebesgue_integral_def)

Theorem (Integral over Closed Interval):
If \(a \leq b\), then the integral of a function \(f\) over the interval \([a, b]\) is equal to the integral of \(f\) over the closed interval from \(a\) to \(b\), expressed as \(\int_{a}^{b} f(x) dx = \int_{a}^{\text{ereal}(b)} f(\text{real}(x)) dx\).

lemma interval_integral_Icc':
  "a ≤ b ⟹ (LBINT x=a..b. f x) = (LBINT x : {x. a ≤ ereal x ∧ ereal x ≤ b}. f x)"
  by (auto intro!: set_integral_discrete_difference[where X="{real_of_ereal a, real_of_ereal b}"]
           simp add: interval_lebesgue_integral_def einterval_iff)

Theorem (Finite Interval Integral and Fundamental Theorem of Calculus):
Given a continuous real-valued function \( f \) defined on a closed interval \([a, b]\), the definite integral of \( f \) from \( a \) to \( b \) is equal to the difference in the values of a function \( F \) that has a vector derivative at every point in \([a, b]\), evaluated at the endpoints of the interval. Mathematically, this is expressed as \(\int_a^b f(x) \, dx = F(b) - F(a)\).

lemma interval_integral_FTC_finite:
  fixes f F :: "real ⇒ 'a::euclidean_space" and a b :: real
  assumes f: "continuous_on {min a b..max a b} f"
  assumes F: "⋀x. min a b ≤ x ⟹ x ≤ max a b ⟹ (F has_vector_derivative (f x)) (at x within
    {min a b..max a b})"
  shows "(LBINT x=a..b. f x) = F b - F a"
proof (cases "a ≤ b")
  case True
  have "(LBINT x=a..b. f x) = (LBINT x. indicat_real {a..b} x *⇩R f x)"
    by (simp add: True interval_integral_Icc set_lebesgue_integral_def)
  also have "… = F b - F a"
  proof (rule integral_FTC_atLeastAtMost [OF True])
    show "continuous_on {a..b} f"
      using True f by linarith
    show "⋀x. ⟦a ≤ x; x ≤ b⟧ ⟹ (F has_vector_derivative f x) (at x within {a..b})"
      by (metis F True max.commute max_absorb1 min_def)
  qed
  finally show ?thesis .
next
  case False
  then have "b ≤ a"
    by simp
  have "- interval_lebesgue_integral lborel (ereal b) (ereal a) f = - (LBINT x. indicat_real {b..a} x *⇩R f x)"
    by (simp add: ‹b ≤ a› interval_integral_Icc set_lebesgue_integral_def)
  also have "… = F b - F a"
  proof (subst integral_FTC_atLeastAtMost [OF ‹b ≤ a›])
    show "continuous_on {b..a} f"
      using False f by linarith
    show "⋀x. ⟦b ≤ x; x ≤ a⟧
         ⟹ (F has_vector_derivative f x) (at x within {b..a})"
      by (metis F False max_def min_def)
  qed auto
  finally show ?thesis
    by (metis interval_integral_endpoints_reverse)
qed

Theorem (Fundamental Theorem of Calculus for Integration):
Given a continuous function \(f\) on an interval \([a, b]\), the integral of its derivative \(f'\) from \(a\) to \(b\) is equal to the difference \(f(b) - f(a)\).

lemma fundamental_theorem_of_calculus:
  assumes "a ≤ b"
  assumes f': "∀x. a ≤ x ∧ x ≤ b ⟶ DERIV f x :> f'(x)"
  shows "Integral (a, b) f' (f(b) - f(a))"
proof (cases "a = b")
  assume "a = b" thus ?thesis by simp
next
  assume "a ≠ b" with ‹a ≤ b› have "a < b" by simp
  show ?thesis
  proof (simp add: Integral_def2, clarify)
    fix e :: real assume "0 < e"
    with ‹a < b› have "0 < e / (b - a)" by simp

    from lemma_straddle [OF f' this]
    obtain δ where "gauge {a..b} δ"
      and δ: "⟦a ≤ u; u ≤ x; x ≤ v; v ≤ b; v - u < δ x⟧ ⟹
           ¦f v - f u - f' x * (v - u)¦ ≤ e * (v - u) / (b - a)" for x u v by auto

    have "∀D. fine δ (a, b) D ⟶ ¦rsum D f' - (f b - f a)¦ ≤ e"
    proof (clarify)
      fix D assume D: "fine δ (a, b) D"
      hence "(∑(u, x, v)←D. f v - f u) = f b - f a"
        by (rule fine_sum_list_eq_diff)
      hence "¦rsum D f' - (f b - f a)¦ = ¦rsum D f' - (∑(u, x, v)←D. f v - f u)¦"
        by simp
      also have "… = ¦(∑(u, x, v)←D. f v - f u) - rsum D f'¦"
        by (rule abs_minus_commute)
      also have "… = ¦∑(u, x, v)←D. (f v - f u) - f' x * (v - u)¦"
        by (simp only: rsum_def sum_list_subtractf split_def)
      also have "… ≤ (∑(u, x, v)←D. ¦(f v - f u) - f' x * (v - u)¦)"
        by (rule ord_le_eq_trans [OF sum_list_abs], simp add: o_def split_def)
      also have "… ≤ (∑(u, x, v)←D. (e / (b - a)) * (v - u))"
        apply (rule sum_list_mono, clarify, rename_tac u x v)
        using D apply (simp add: δ mem_fine mem_fine2 mem_fine3)
        done
      also have "… = e"
        using fine_sum_list_eq_diff [OF D, where f="λx. x"]
        unfolding split_def sum_list_const_mult
        using ‹a < b› by simp
      finally show "¦rsum D f' - (f b - f a)¦ ≤ e" .
    qed

    with ‹gauge {a..b} δ›
    show "∃δ. gauge {a..b} δ ∧ (∀D. fine δ (a, b) D ⟶ ¦rsum D f' - (f b - f a)¦ ≤ e)"
      by auto
  qed
qed

Theorem (Integral Difference of Intervals):
Given a continuous real-valued function \(f\) on a Banach space, if \(c \geq a\) and \(c \geq b\), then the integral of \(f\) over the interval from \(a\) to \(c\) minus the integral of \(f\) over the interval from \(b\) to \(c\) equals the integral of \(f\) over the interval from \(a\) to \(b\) if \(a \leq b\), or the negative of the integral of \(f\) over the interval from \(b\) to \(a\) if \(b > a\).
Mathematically, \(\int_{a}^{c} f \, dx - \int_{b}^{c} f \, dx = \int_{a}^{b} f \, dx\) if \(a \leq b\), and \(-\int_{b}^{a} f \, dx\) if \(b > a\).

lemma integral_minus_sets':
  fixes f::"real ⇒ 'a::banach"
  shows "c ≥ a ⟹ c ≥ b ⟹ f integrable_on {min a b .. c} ⟹
    integral {a .. c} f - integral {b .. c} f =
    (if a ≤ b then integral {a .. b} f else - integral {b .. a} f)"
  using integral_combine[of b a c f] integral_combine[of a b c f]
  by (auto simp: algebra_simps min_def)

Theorem (Interval Integral of a Function):
If \(a \leq b\), then the integral of a function \(f\) over the interval \([a, b]\) is equal to the integral of \(f\) over the set of real numbers between \(a\) and \(b\), formally \(\int_{a}^{b} f(x) dx = \int_{\mathbb{R}_{a}^{b}} f(x) dx\).

lemma interval_integral_Ioc':
  "a ≤ b ⟹ (LBINT x=a..b. f x) = (LBINT x : {x. a < ereal x ∧ ereal x ≤ b}. f x)"
  by (auto intro!: set_integral_discrete_difference[where X="{real_of_ereal a, real_of_ereal b}"]
           simp add: interval_lebesgue_integral_def einterval_iff)

Theorem (Interval Integral Equivalence):
If \(a \leq b\), then the integral of a function \(f\) over the interval \([a, b]\) is equivalent to the integral of \(f\) over the set of all points between \(a\) and \(b\), formally \(\int_{a}^{b} f(x) dx = \int_{a}^{b} f(x)\).

lemma interval_integral_Ioc:
  "a ≤ b ⟹ (LBINT x=a..b. f x) = (LBINT x : {a<..b}. f x)"
  by (auto intro!: set_integral_discrete_difference[where X="{a, b}"]
           simp add: interval_lebesgue_integral_def einterval_iff)

Theorem (Integral over Closed Interval):
If \(a \leq b\), then the integral of a function \(f\) over the closed interval \([a, b]\) is equal to the integral over the open interval \((a, b)\), formally \(\int_{a}^{b} f(x) dx = \int_{a}^{b} f(x) dx\).

lemma interval_integral_Ico:
  "a ≤ b ⟹ (LBINT x=a..b. f x) = (LBINT x : {a..<b}. f x)"
  by (auto intro!: set_integral_discrete_difference[where X="{a, b}"]
           simp add: interval_lebesgue_integral_def einterval_iff)

Theorem (Integral of a Continuous and Non-Negative Function on an Interval):
Given a real-valued function \( f \) that is continuous and non-negative on the interval \([a, b]\), the integral of \( f \) over this interval is equal to the difference between the values of a certain function \( B \) and \( A \) evaluated at the endpoints \( a \) and \( b \), respectively. Formally, the integral of \( f \) from \( a \) to \( b \) is expressed as \( \int_a^b f(x) \, dx = B(b) - A(a) \).

lemma interval_integral_FTC_nonneg:
  fixes f F :: "real ⇒ real" and a b :: ereal
  assumes "a < b"
  assumes F: "⋀x. a < ereal x ⟹ ereal x < b ⟹ DERIV F x :> f x"
  assumes f: "⋀x. a < ereal x ⟹ ereal x < b ⟹ isCont f x"
  assumes f_nonneg: "AE x in lborel. a < ereal x ⟶ ereal x < b ⟶ 0 ≤ f x"
  assumes A: "((F ∘ real_of_ereal) ⤏ A) (at_right a)"
  assumes B: "((F ∘ real_of_ereal) ⤏ B) (at_left b)"
  shows
    "set_integrable lborel (einterval a b) f"
    "(LBINT x=a..b. f x) = B - A"
proof -
  obtain u l where approx:
    "einterval a b = (⋃i. {l i .. u i})"
    "incseq u" "decseq l" "⋀i. l i < u i" "⋀i. a < l i" "⋀i. u i < b"
    "l ⇢ a" "u ⇢ b" 
    by (blast intro: einterval_Icc_approximation[OF ‹a < b›])
  have aless[simp]: "⋀x i. l i ≤ x ⟹ a < ereal x"
    by (rule order_less_le_trans, rule approx, force)
  have lessb[simp]: "⋀x i. x ≤ u i ⟹ ereal x < b"
    by (rule order_le_less_trans, subst ereal_less_eq(3), assumption, rule approx)
  have cf: "⋀i. continuous_on {min (l i) (u i)..max (l i) (u i)} f"
    using approx f by (intro continuous_at_imp_continuous_on strip) auto
  have FTCi: "⋀i. (LBINT x=l i..u i. f x) = F (u i) - F (l i)"
    apply (intro interval_integral_FTC_finite cf DERIV_subset [OF F])
    by (smt (verit) F aless approx(4) has_real_derivative_iff_has_vector_derivative has_vector_derivative_at_within lessb)
  have 1: "⋀i. set_integrable lborel {l i..u i} f"
    by (meson aless lessb assms(3) atLeastAtMost_iff borel_integrable_atLeastAtMost' continuous_at_imp_continuous_on)
  have 2: "set_borel_measurable lborel (einterval a b) f"
    unfolding set_borel_measurable_def
    by (auto simp del: real_scaleR_def intro!: borel_measurable_continuous_on_indicator
             simp: continuous_on_eq_continuous_at einterval_iff f)
  have "(λx. F (l x)) ⇢ A"
    using A approx unfolding tendsto_at_iff_sequentially comp_def
    by (force elim!: allE[of _ "λi. ereal (l i)"])
  moreover have "(λx. F (u x)) ⇢ B"
    using B approx unfolding tendsto_at_iff_sequentially comp_def
    by (force elim!: allE[of _ "λi. ereal (u i)"])
  ultimately have 3: "(λi. LBINT x=l i..u i. f x) ⇢ B - A"
    by (simp add: FTCi tendsto_diff)
  show "(LBINT x=a..b. f x) = B - A"
    by (rule interval_integral_Icc_approx_nonneg [OF ‹a < b› approx 1 f_nonneg 2 3])
  show "set_integrable lborel (einterval a b) f"
    by (rule interval_integral_Icc_approx_nonneg [OF ‹a < b› approx 1 f_nonneg 2 3])
qed

Theorem (Differentiation and Integration Inverse Relationship): 
The process of finding the derivative, which involves calculating rates of change for functions at specific points, can be reversed through integration. This reverse operation reconstructs a function from its rate of changes over an interval, demonstrating that differentiation and integration are inverse processes in calculus.

Theorem (Fundamental Theorem of Calculus for IVP):
Given a real-valued function \( f \) that has a derivative on a closed interval \([a, b]\), the integral of \( f' \) from \( a \) to \( b \) equals the difference \( f(b) - f(a) \). This theorem connects differentiation and integration, asserting that the integral of a derivative function over an interval gives the net change in the original function over that interval.

lemma fundamental_theorem_of_calculus_ivl_integral:
  fixes f :: "real ⇒ 'a::banach"
  shows "(f has_vderiv_on f') (closed_segment a b) ⟹ (f' has_ivl_integral f b - f a) a b"
  by (auto simp: has_ivl_integral_def closed_segment_eq_real_ivl intro!: fundamental_theorem_of_calculus')

Theorem (Fundamental Theorem of Calculus for Integrable Functions on an Interval):
Given a real-valued function \( f \) that is continuous and differentiable on the interval \([a, b]\), and integrable over that interval, the definite integral of \( f \) from \( a \) to \( b \) equals the difference between the values of its antiderivative at \( b \) and \( a \), expressed as \(\int_a^b f(x) \, dx = F(b) - F(a)\), where \( F \) is the antiderivative of \( f \).

theorem interval_integral_FTC_integrable:
  fixes f F :: "real ⇒ 'a::euclidean_space" and a b :: ereal
  assumes "a < b"
  assumes F: "⋀x. a < ereal x ⟹ ereal x < b ⟹ (F has_vector_derivative f x) (at x)"
  assumes f: "⋀x. a < ereal x ⟹ ereal x < b ⟹ isCont f x"
  assumes f_integrable: "set_integrable lborel (einterval a b) f"
  assumes A: "((F ∘ real_of_ereal) ⤏ A) (at_right a)"
  assumes B: "((F ∘ real_of_ereal) ⤏ B) (at_left b)"
  shows "(LBINT x=a..b. f x) = B - A"
proof -
  obtain u l where approx:
    "einterval a b = (⋃i. {l i .. u i})"
    "incseq u" "decseq l" "⋀i. l i < u i" "⋀i. a < l i" "⋀i. u i < b"
    "l ⇢ a" "u ⇢ b" 
    by (blast intro: einterval_Icc_approximation[OF ‹a < b›])
  have [simp]: "⋀x i. l i ≤ x ⟹ a < ereal x"
    by (rule order_less_le_trans, rule approx, force)
  have [simp]: "⋀x i. x ≤ u i ⟹ ereal x < b"
    by (rule order_le_less_trans, subst ereal_less_eq(3), assumption, rule approx)
  have FTCi: "⋀i. (LBINT x=l i..u i. f x) = F (u i) - F (l i)"
    using assms approx
    by (auto simp: less_imp_le min_def max_def
             intro!: f continuous_at_imp_continuous_on interval_integral_FTC_finite
             intro: has_vector_derivative_at_within)
  have "(λi. LBINT x=l i..u i. f x) ⇢ B - A"
    unfolding FTCi
  proof (intro tendsto_intros)
    show "(λx. F (l x)) ⇢ A"
      using A approx unfolding tendsto_at_iff_sequentially comp_def
      by (elim allE[of _ "λi. ereal (l i)"], auto)
    show "(λx. F (u x)) ⇢ B"
      using B approx unfolding tendsto_at_iff_sequentially comp_def
      by (elim allE[of _ "λi. ereal (u i)"], auto)
  qed
  moreover have "(λi. LBINT x=l i..u i. f x) ⇢ (LBINT x=a..b. f x)"
    by (rule interval_integral_Icc_approx_integrable [OF ‹a < b› approx f_integrable])
  ultimately show ?thesis
    by (elim LIMSEQ_unique)
qed

Theorem (Integral of the Inverse of a Positive Function):
Given a real-valued function \( f \) that is positive, continuous, and differentiable on the interval \([a, b]\), with \( f(x) > 0 \) for all \( x \) in \([a, b]\), the integral of the function \( \frac{f'(x)}{f(x)} \) from \( a \) to \( b \) is equal to the natural logarithm of \( f(b) \) minus the natural logarithm of \( f(a) \), that is, \(\int_a^b \frac{f'(x)}{f(x)} dx = \ln(f(b)) - \ln(f(a))\).

lemma inverse_fun_has_integral_ln:
  fixes f :: "real ⇒ real" and f' :: "real ⇒ real"
  assumes "a ≤ b" and
    "⋀x. x∈{a..b} ⟹ f x > 0" and
    "continuous_on {a..b} f" and 
    "⋀x. x∈{a<..<b} ⟹ (f has_real_derivative f' x) (at x)"
  shows "((λx. f' x / f x) has_integral (ln (f b) - ln (f a))) {a..b}"
proof -
  have "continuous_on {a..b} (λx. ln (f x))" using assms by (intro continuous_intros; force)
  moreover have "⋀x. x∈{a<..<b} ⟹ ((λx. ln (f x)) has_vector_derivative f' x / f x) (at x)"
    apply (rewrite has_real_derivative_iff_has_vector_derivative[THEN sym])
    using assms by (intro DERIV_ln_divide_chain; simp)
  ultimately show ?thesis using assms by (intro fundamental_theorem_of_calculus_interior; simp)
qed

Theorem (Integration of the nth Derivative of a Function):
Given a function \( f \), the integral of the nth derivative of \( f \) with respect to \( f \) itself is equal to the original function, that is, \( \int (\text{fds\_nth} f 1) (\text{fds\_deriv} f) \, df = f \).

lemma fds_integral_fds_deriv [simp]: "fds_integral (fds_nth f 1) (fds_deriv f) = f"
  by (simp add: fds_deriv_def fds_integral_def fds_eq_iff)

Theorem (Inverse of the Derivative of a Function):
Given a differentiable function \(f\) that does not vanish at a point \(x\), the derivative of the inverse function at \(x\) is the negative reciprocal of the derivative of \(f\) at \(x\), formally \(\frac{d}{dx} \left( \frac{1}{f(x)} \right) = -\frac{1}{f'(x)}\).

lemma GDERIV_inverse:
    "⟦GDERIV f x :> df; f x ≠ 0⟧
     ⟹ GDERIV (λx. inverse (f x)) x :> - (inverse (f x))⇧2 *⇩R df"
  by (metis DERIV_inverse GDERIV_DERIV_compose numerals(2))

Theorem (Fundamental Theorem of Calculus for ODEs):
Given a function \( f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathcal{B} \) (where \( \mathcal{B} \) is a Banach space), if \( a \leq b \), then for \( f \) having a derivative on \( f' \), the integral of \( f' \) from \( a \) to \( b \) equals \( f(b) - f(a) \).

lemma fundamental_theorem_of_calculus':
  fixes f :: "real ⇒ 'a::banach"
  shows "a ≤ b ⟹ (f has_vderiv_on f') {a .. b} ⟹ (f' has_integral (f b - f a)) {a .. b}"
  by (auto intro!: fundamental_theorem_of_calculus simp: has_vderiv_on_def)

Theorem (Derivative of Left and Right Inverses):
Given a function \(f\) with left and right inverses \(x\) and \(y\) respectively, such that the subderivative of \(f\) at \(x\) and \(y\) equals 1, the derivative of the left inverse \(fls_left_inverse f x\) and the right inverse \(fls_right_inverse f y\) with respect to \(f\) are related by the product of the inverses and the derivative of \(f\). Specifically, \(\frac{d}{dx}(fls_left_inverse f x) = -fls_left_inverse f x \cdot \frac{d}{dx}f \cdot fls_left_inverse f x\) and \(\frac{d}{dy}(fls_right_inverse f y) = -fls_right_inverse f y \cdot \frac{d}{dy}f \cdot fls_right_inverse f y\).

lemma fls_deriv_lr_inverse:
  assumes "x * f $$ fls_subdegree f = 1" "f $$ fls_subdegree f * y = 1"
  ― ‹These assumptions imply x equals y, but no need to assume that.›
  shows   "fls_deriv (fls_left_inverse f x) =
            - fls_left_inverse f x * fls_deriv f * fls_left_inverse f x"
  and     "fls_deriv (fls_right_inverse f y) =
            - fls_right_inverse f y * fls_deriv f * fls_right_inverse f y"
proof-

  define L where "L ≡ fls_left_inverse f x"
  hence "fls_deriv (L * f) = 0" using fls_left_inverse[OF assms(1)] by simp
  with assms show "fls_deriv L = - L * fls_deriv f * L"
    using fls_right_inverse'[OF assms]
    by    (simp add: minus_unique mult.assoc L_def)

  define R where "R ≡ fls_right_inverse f y"
  hence "fls_deriv (f * R) = 0" using fls_right_inverse[OF assms(2)] by simp
  hence 1: "f * fls_deriv R + fls_deriv f * R = 0" by simp
  have "R * f * fls_deriv R = - R * fls_deriv f * R"
    using iffD2[OF eq_neg_iff_add_eq_0, OF 1] by (simp add: mult.assoc)
  thus "fls_deriv R = - R * fls_deriv f * R"
    using fls_left_inverse'[OF assms] by (simp add: R_def)

qed

Theorem (Substitution and Integration of Polynomials):
Given a real-valued function \( f \) and a continuous, non-decreasing function \( g \) on the interval \([a, b]\), where \( a < b \), and both \( f \) and \( g \) are integrable over \([a, b]\), the integral of \( f \) composed with \( g \) over \([a, b]\) equals the integral of the derivative of \( g \) times \( f \) composed with \( g \) over the same interval.

Mathematically, this is expressed as:
\[
\int_a^b f(g(x)) \, dx = \int_a^b g'(x) \cdot f(g(x)) \, dx
\]

This theorem assumes that \( g \) is differentiable and its derivative \( g' \) is non-negative on \([a, b]\).

theorem interval_integral_substitution_integrable:
  fixes f :: "real ⇒ 'a::euclidean_space" and a b u v :: ereal
  assumes "a < b"
  and deriv_g: "⋀x. a < ereal x ⟹ ereal x < b ⟹ DERIV g x :> g' x"
  and contf: "⋀x. a < ereal x ⟹ ereal x < b ⟹ isCont f (g x)"
  and contg': "⋀x. a < ereal x ⟹ ereal x < b ⟹ isCont g' x"
  and g'_nonneg: "⋀x. a ≤ ereal x ⟹ ereal x ≤ b ⟹ 0 ≤ g' x"
  and A: "((ereal ∘ g ∘ real_of_ereal) ⤏ A) (at_right a)"
  and B: "((ereal ∘ g ∘ real_of_ereal) ⤏ B) (at_left b)"
  and integrable: "set_integrable lborel (einterval a b) (λx. g' x *⇩R f (g x))"
  and integrable2: "set_integrable lborel (einterval A B) (λx. f x)"
  shows "(LBINT x=A..B. f x) = (LBINT x=a..b. g' x *⇩R f (g x))"
proof -
  obtain u l where approx [simp]:
    "einterval a b = (⋃i. {l i .. u i})"
    "incseq u" "decseq l" "⋀i. l i < u i" "⋀i. a < l i" "⋀i. u i < b"
    "l ⇢ a" "u ⇢ b" 
    by (blast intro: einterval_Icc_approximation[OF ‹a < b›])
  note less_imp_le [simp]
  have [simp]: "⋀x i. l i ≤ x ⟹ a < ereal x"
    by (rule order_less_le_trans, rule approx, force)
  have [simp]: "⋀x i. x ≤ u i ⟹ ereal x < b"
    by (rule order_le_less_trans, subst ereal_less_eq(3), assumption, rule approx)
  then have lessb[simp]: "⋀i. l i < b"
    using approx(4) less_eq_real_def by blast
  have [simp]: "⋀i. a < u i"
    by (rule order_less_trans, rule approx, auto, rule approx)
  have lle[simp]: "⋀i j. i ≤ j ⟹ l j ≤ l i" by (rule decseqD, rule approx)
  have [simp]: "⋀i j. i ≤ j ⟹ u i ≤ u j" by (rule incseqD, rule approx)
  have g_nondec [simp]: "g x ≤ g y" if "a < x" "x ≤ y" "y < b" for x y
  proof (rule DERIV_nonneg_imp_nondecreasing [OF ‹x ≤ y›], intro exI conjI)
    show "⋀u. x ≤ u ⟹ u ≤ y ⟹ (g has_real_derivative g' u) (at u)"
      by (meson deriv_g ereal_less_eq(3) le_less_trans less_le_trans that)
    show "⋀u. x ≤ u ⟹ u ≤ y ⟹ 0 ≤ g' u"
      by (meson assms(5) dual_order.trans le_ereal_le less_imp_le order_refl that)
  qed
  have "A ≤ B" and un: "einterval A B = (⋃i. {g(l i)<..<g(u i)})"
  proof -
    have A2: "(λi. g (l i)) ⇢ A"
      using A apply (auto simp: einterval_def tendsto_at_iff_sequentially comp_def)
      by (drule_tac x = "λi. ereal (l i)" in spec, auto)
    hence A3: "⋀i. g (l i) ≥ A"
      by (intro decseq_ge, auto simp: decseq_def)
    have B2: "(λi. g (u i)) ⇢ B"
      using B apply (auto simp: einterval_def tendsto_at_iff_sequentially comp_def)
      by (drule_tac x = "λi. ereal (u i)" in spec, auto)
    hence B3: "⋀i. g (u i) ≤ B"
      by (intro incseq_le, auto simp: incseq_def)
    have "ereal (g (l 0)) ≤ ereal (g (u 0))"
      by auto
    then show "A ≤ B"
      by (meson A3 B3 order.trans)
    { fix x :: real
      assume "A < x" and "x < B"
      then have "eventually (λi. ereal (g (l i)) < x ∧ x < ereal (g (u i))) sequentially"
        by (fast intro: eventually_conj order_tendstoD A2 B2)
      hence "∃i. g (l i) < x ∧ x < g (u i)"
        by (simp add: eventually_sequentially, auto)
    } note AB = this
    show "einterval A B = (⋃i. {g(l i)<..<g(u i)})"
    proof
      show "einterval A B ⊆ (⋃i. {g(l i)<..<g(u i)})"
        by (auto simp: einterval_def AB)
      show "(⋃i. {g(l i)<..<g(u i)}) ⊆ einterval A B"
      proof (clarsimp simp add: einterval_def, intro conjI)
        show "⋀x i. ⟦g (l i) < x; x < g (u i)⟧ ⟹ A < ereal x"
          using A3 le_ereal_less by blast
        show "⋀x i. ⟦g (l i) < x; x < g (u i)⟧ ⟹ ereal x < B"
          using B3 ereal_le_less by blast
      qed
    qed
  qed
  (* finally, the main argument *)
  have eq1: "(LBINT x=l i.. u i. g' x *⇩R f (g x)) = (LBINT y=g (l i)..g (u i). f y)" for i
    apply (rule interval_integral_substitution_finite [OF _ DERIV_subset [OF deriv_g]])
    unfolding has_real_derivative_iff_has_vector_derivative[symmetric]
         apply (auto intro!: continuous_at_imp_continuous_on contf contg')
    done
  have "(λi. LBINT x=l i..u i. g' x *⇩R f (g x)) ⇢ (LBINT x=a..b. g' x *⇩R f (g x))"
    using approx(4) ‹a < b› integrable interval_integral_Icc_approx_integrable by fastforce
  hence 2: "(λi. (LBINT y=g (l i)..g (u i). f y)) ⇢ (LBINT x=a..b. g' x *⇩R f (g x))"
    by (simp add: eq1)
  have incseq: "incseq (λi. {g (l i)<..<g (u i)})"
    apply (clarsimp simp: incseq_def, intro conjI)
    using lessb lle approx(5) g_nondec le_less_trans apply blast
    by (force intro: less_le_trans)
  have "(λi. set_lebesgue_integral lborel {g (l i)<..<g (u i)} f)
        ⇢ set_lebesgue_integral lborel (einterval A B) f"
    unfolding un  by (rule set_integral_cont_up) (use incseq  integrable2 un in auto)
  then have "(λi. (LBINT y=g (l i)..g (u i). f y)) ⇢ (LBINT x = A..B. f x)"
    by (simp add: interval_lebesgue_integral_le_eq ‹A ≤ B›)
  thus ?thesis by (intro LIMSEQ_unique [OF _ 2])
qed

Theorem (Derivative of the Inverse Function):
Given a function \( f \) from an open subset \( S \) of a Euclidean space, which has a derivative at every point in \( S \), and an inverse function \( g \) such that \( g(f(x)) = x \) for all \( x \) in \( S \), and the composition of the derivatives \( f' \circ g' \) equals the identity function, then the inverse function \( g \) also has a derivative at every point in \( S \).

theorem has_derivative_inverse_on:
  fixes f :: "'n::euclidean_space ⇒ 'n"
  assumes "open S"
    and "⋀x. x ∈ S ⟹ (f has_derivative f'(x)) (at x)"
    and "⋀x. x ∈ S ⟹ g (f x) = x"
    and "f' x ∘ g' x = id"
    and "x ∈ S"
  shows "(g has_derivative g'(x)) (at (f x))"
  by (meson assms continuous_on_eq_continuous_at has_derivative_continuous has_derivative_inverse_strong)

Theorem (Fundamental Theorem of Calculus for Integration):
Given a continuous function \(f\) on an interval \([a, b]\), the integral of its derivative \(f'\) from \(a\) to \(b\) is equal to the difference \(f(b) - f(a)\).

lemma fundamental_theorem_of_calculus:
  assumes "a ≤ b"
  assumes f': "∀x. a ≤ x ∧ x ≤ b ⟶ DERIV f x :> f'(x)"
  shows "Integral (a, b) f' (f(b) - f(a))"
proof (cases "a = b")
  assume "a = b" thus ?thesis by simp
next
  assume "a ≠ b" with ‹a ≤ b› have "a < b" by simp
  show ?thesis
  proof (simp add: Integral_def2, clarify)
    fix e :: real assume "0 < e"
    with ‹a < b› have "0 < e / (b - a)" by simp

    from lemma_straddle [OF f' this]
    obtain δ where "gauge {a..b} δ"
      and δ: "⟦a ≤ u; u ≤ x; x ≤ v; v ≤ b; v - u < δ x⟧ ⟹
           ¦f v - f u - f' x * (v - u)¦ ≤ e * (v - u) / (b - a)" for x u v by auto

    have "∀D. fine δ (a, b) D ⟶ ¦rsum D f' - (f b - f a)¦ ≤ e"
    proof (clarify)
      fix D assume D: "fine δ (a, b) D"
      hence "(∑(u, x, v)←D. f v - f u) = f b - f a"
        by (rule fine_sum_list_eq_diff)
      hence "¦rsum D f' - (f b - f a)¦ = ¦rsum D f' - (∑(u, x, v)←D. f v - f u)¦"
        by simp
      also have "… = ¦(∑(u, x, v)←D. f v - f u) - rsum D f'¦"
        by (rule abs_minus_commute)
      also have "… = ¦∑(u, x, v)←D. (f v - f u) - f' x * (v - u)¦"
        by (simp only: rsum_def sum_list_subtractf split_def)
      also have "… ≤ (∑(u, x, v)←D. ¦(f v - f u) - f' x * (v - u)¦)"
        by (rule ord_le_eq_trans [OF sum_list_abs], simp add: o_def split_def)
      also have "… ≤ (∑(u, x, v)←D. (e / (b - a)) * (v - u))"
        apply (rule sum_list_mono, clarify, rename_tac u x v)
        using D apply (simp add: δ mem_fine mem_fine2 mem_fine3)
        done
      also have "… = e"
        using fine_sum_list_eq_diff [OF D, where f="λx. x"]
        unfolding split_def sum_list_const_mult
        using ‹a < b› by simp
      finally show "¦rsum D f' - (f b - f a)¦ ≤ e" .
    qed

    with ‹gauge {a..b} δ›
    show "∃δ. gauge {a..b} δ ∧ (∀D. fine δ (a, b) D ⟶ ¦rsum D f' - (f b - f a)¦ ≤ e)"
      by auto
  qed
qed

This theorem provides insights into how to integrate and differentiate functions with respect to their inverses.

top_results.embedding_string:
Theorem (Inverse of the Derivative of a Function):
Given a differentiable function \(f\) that does not vanish at a point \(x\), the derivative of the inverse function at \(x\) is the negative reciprocal of the derivative of \(f\) at \(x\), formally \(\frac{d}{dx} \left( \frac{1}{f(x)} \right) = -\frac{1}{f'(x)}\).

lemma GDERIV_inverse:
    "⟦GDERIV f x :> df; f x ≠ 0⟧
     ⟹ GDERIV (λx. inverse (f x)) x :> - (inverse (f x))⇧2 *⇩R df"
  by (metis DERIV_inverse GDERIV_DERIV_compose numerals(2))

Theorem (Derivative of the Inverse Function):
Given a function \( f \) from an open subset \( S \) of a Euclidean space, which has a derivative at every point in \( S \), and an inverse function \( g \) such that \( g(f(x)) = x \) for all \( x \) in \( S \), and the composition of the derivatives \( f' \circ g' \) equals the identity function, then the inverse function \( g \) also has a derivative at every point in \( S \).

theorem has_derivative_inverse_on:
  fixes f :: "'n::euclidean_space ⇒ 'n"
  assumes "open S"
    and "⋀x. x ∈ S ⟹ (f has_derivative f'(x)) (at x)"
    and "⋀x. x ∈ S ⟹ g (f x) = x"
    and "f' x ∘ g' x = id"
    and "x ∈ S"
  shows "(g has_derivative g'(x)) (at (f x))"
  by (meson assms continuous_on_eq_continuous_at has_derivative_continuous has_derivative_inverse_strong)

Theorem (Integral of the Inverse of a Positive Function):
Given a real-valued function \( f \) that is positive, continuous, and differentiable on the interval \([a, b]\), with \( f(x) > 0 \) for all \( x \) in \([a, b]\), the integral of the function \( \frac{f'(x)}{f(x)} \) from \( a \) to \( b \) is equal to the natural logarithm of \( f(b) \) minus the natural logarithm of \( f(a) \), that is, \(\int_a^b \frac{f'(x)}{f(x)} dx = \ln(f(b)) - \ln(f(a))\).

lemma inverse_fun_has_integral_ln:
  fixes f :: "real ⇒ real" and f' :: "real ⇒ real"
  assumes "a ≤ b" and
    "⋀x. x∈{a..b} ⟹ f x > 0" and
    "continuous_on {a..b} f" and 
    "⋀x. x∈{a<..<b} ⟹ (f has_real_derivative f' x) (at x)"
  shows "((λx. f' x / f x) has_integral (ln (f b) - ln (f a))) {a..b}"
proof -
  have "continuous_on {a..b} (λx. ln (f x))" using assms by (intro continuous_intros; force)
  moreover have "⋀x. x∈{a<..<b} ⟹ ((λx. ln (f x)) has_vector_derivative f' x / f x) (at x)"
    apply (rewrite has_real_derivative_iff_has_vector_derivative[THEN sym])
    using assms by (intro DERIV_ln_divide_chain; simp)
  ultimately show ?thesis using assms by (intro fundamental_theorem_of_calculus_interior; simp)
qed

Theorem (Derivative of the Inverse Function):
Given a real-valued function \( f \) with a derivative at a point \( x \), a bounded linear function \( g' \) that is the derivative of an inverse function \( g \), and the conditions that \( g' \circ f' = \text{id} \), \( g \) is continuous at \( f(x) \), \( g(f(x)) = x \), and \( f(x) \) lies in a topological space \( T \) where \( f \) maps \( T \) into itself and preserves the identity, we can conclude that \( g \) also has a derivative at \( f(x) \).

lemma has_derivative_inverse_basic_x:
  fixes f :: "'a::real_normed_vector ⇒ 'b::real_normed_vector"
  assumes "(f has_derivative f') (at x)"
    and "bounded_linear g'"
    and "g' ∘ f' = id"
    and "continuous (at (f x)) g"
    and "g (f x) = x"
    and "open T"
    and "f x ∈ T"
    and "⋀y. y ∈ T ⟹ f (g y) = y"
  shows "(g has_derivative g') (at (f x))"
  by (rule has_derivative_inverse_basic) (use assms in auto)

Theorem (Derivative of the Inverse Function):
Given a real-normed vector function f that is continuous and has a bounded linear derivative at a point x, and an inverse function g that satisfies g composed with f' equals the identity at x, then g also has a derivative at the point f(x), and this derivative is the inverse of f' at x.

lemma has_derivative_inverse_dieudonne:
  fixes f :: "'a::real_normed_vector ⇒ 'b::real_normed_vector"
  assumes "open S"
    and fS: "open (f ` S)"
    and A: "continuous_on S f" "continuous_on (f ` S) g" 
           "⋀x. x ∈ S ⟹ g (f x) = x" "x ∈ S"
    and B: "(f has_derivative f') (at x)" "bounded_linear g'" "g' ∘ f' = id"
  shows "(g has_derivative g') (at (f x))"
  using A fS continuous_on_eq_continuous_at
  by (intro has_derivative_inverse_basic_x[OF B _ _ fS]) force+

Theorem (Derivative Inverse Function):
Given a function \(f\) with a field derivative \(d\) at a point \(x\), if \(f(x)\) is not zero, then the inverse function of \(f\) at \(x\) has a derivative that is the negative product of \(d\) and the derivative of the inverse function of \(f(x)\) raised to the power of \(Suc(Suc(0))\).

lemma DERIV_inverse_fun:
  "(f has_field_derivative d) (at x within s) ⟹ f x ≠ 0 ⟹
    ((λx. inverse (f x)) has_field_derivative (- (d * inverse(f x ^ Suc (Suc 0))))) (at x within s)"
  by (drule (1) DERIV_inverse') (simp add: ac_simps nonzero_inverse_mult_distrib)

Theorem (Fundamental Theorem of Calculus for IVP):
Given a real-valued function \( f \) that has a derivative on a closed interval \([a, b]\), the integral of \( f' \) from \( a \) to \( b \) equals the difference \( f(b) - f(a) \). This theorem connects differentiation and integration, asserting that the integral of a derivative function over an interval gives the net change in the original function over that interval.

lemma fundamental_theorem_of_calculus_ivl_integral:
  fixes f :: "real ⇒ 'a::banach"
  shows "(f has_vderiv_on f') (closed_segment a b) ⟹ (f' has_ivl_integral f b - f a) a b"
  by (auto simp: has_ivl_integral_def closed_segment_eq_real_ivl intro!: fundamental_theorem_of_calculus')

Theorem (Derivative of the Inverse Function):
Given a continuous function \( f \) from a Euclidean space to itself, and an inverse function \( g \) that maps \( f(y) \) back to \( y \), if \( f \) has a derivative at a point \( y \), then the inverse function \( g \) also has a derivative at \( y \), and the derivative of \( g \) is the reciprocal of the derivative of \( f \) at \( y \).

lemma has_derivative_inverse_strong_x:
  fixes f :: "'a::euclidean_space ⇒ 'a"
  assumes "open S"
    and "g y ∈ S"
    and "continuous_on S f"
    and "⋀x. x ∈ S ⟹ g (f x) = x"
    and "(f has_derivative f') (at (g y))"
    and "f' ∘ g' = id"
    and f: "f (g y) = y"
  shows "(g has_derivative g') (at y)"
  using has_derivative_inverse_strong[OF assms(1-6)] by (simp add: f)

Theorem (Derivative of the Inverse Function):
Given a differentiable function \( f \) at a point \( x \) where \( f(x) \neq 0 \), the derivative of the inverse function at \( x \) is the reciprocal of the derivative of \( f \) at \( x \) times the derivative of the inverse function at \( f(x) \).

lemma has_derivative_inverse[simp, derivative_intros]:
  fixes f :: "_ ⇒ 'a::real_normed_div_algebra"
  assumes x:  "f x ≠ 0"
    and f: "(f has_derivative f') (at x within S)"
  shows "((λx. inverse (f x)) has_derivative (λh. - (inverse (f x) * f' h * inverse (f x))))
    (at x within S)"
  using has_derivative_compose[OF f has_derivative_inverse', OF x] .

Theorem (Fundamental Theorem of Calculus for ODEs):
Given a function \( f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathcal{B} \) (where \( \mathcal{B} \) is a Banach space), if \( a \leq b \), then for \( f \) having a derivative on \( f' \), the integral of \( f' \) from \( a \) to \( b \) equals \( f(b) - f(a) \).

lemma fundamental_theorem_of_calculus':
  fixes f :: "real ⇒ 'a::banach"
  shows "a ≤ b ⟹ (f has_vderiv_on f') {a .. b} ⟹ (f' has_integral (f b - f a)) {a .. b}"
  by (auto intro!: fundamental_theorem_of_calculus simp: has_vderiv_on_def)

Theorem (Fourier Series Representation of Complex Numbers):
This theorem provides an expression for the nth power of a complex number in polar form, where r is raised to the power of n and cosine and sine functions are used with appropriate angles. It establishes that any complex number can be represented as a sum involving its magnitude (r), angle (θ), and trigonometric components based on powers of these values.

top_results.embedding_string:
Theorem (Fourier Series Representation):
The Fourier series expresses any square-integrable function on the real line as a sum of sines and cosines. Specifically, for a given function, its Fourier series is composed of terms involving sine and cosine functions with frequencies that are integer multiples of a fundamental frequency. The coefficients of these terms are determined by integrating the product of the function and the sine or cosine functions over a period. This representation is particularly useful for analyzing periodic functions and approximating them with a series of simpler trigonometric functions.

lemma trigonometric_set:
  "trigonometric_set 0 x = 1 / sqrt(2 * pi)"
  "trigonometric_set (Suc (2 * n)) x = sin(real(Suc n) * x) / sqrt(pi)"
  "trigonometric_set (2 * n + 2) x = cos(real(Suc n) * x) / sqrt(pi)"
  "trigonometric_set (Suc (Suc (2 * n))) x = cos(real(Suc n) * x) / sqrt(pi)"
  by (simp_all add: trigonometric_set_def algebra_simps add_divide_distrib)

Theorem (DeMoivre's Theorem for Complex Numbers):
Given a complex number in polar form \(rcis(a)\), raising it to an integer power \(n\) results in \(rcis(a)^n = rcis(r^n \cdot a)\), where \(r\) is the magnitude and \(a\) is the argument of the complex number.

lemma DeMoivre2: "(rcis r a) ^ n = rcis (r ^ n) (real n * a)"
  by (simp add: rcis_def power_mult_distrib DeMoivre)

Theorem (Equivalence of Complex Numbers in Terms of Angles):
Given two complex numbers \(a\) and \(b\) such that their complex exponentials are equal (\(cis a = cis b\)), there exists an integer \(k\) for which the difference between \(a\) and \(b\) is equal to \(2\pi k\). This reflects the fact that complex numbers can be represented by angles in the complex plane, and their equivalence corresponds to a full rotation by \(2\pi\) radians.

lemma cis_eq:
  assumes "cis a = cis b"
  shows "∃ k::int. a - b = 2 * k * pi"
  using assms sin_cos_eq[of a b]
  using cis.sel[of a] cis.sel[of b]
  by (cases "cis a", cases "cis b") auto

Theorem (DeMoivre's Theorem for Complex Numbers):
For any complex number \(z\) and integer \(n\), the expression \((\cos(z) + \operatorname{i}\sin(z))^n\) simplifies to \(\cos(nz) + \operatorname{i}\sin(nz)\).

lemma DeMoivre: "(cos z + 𝗂 * sin z) ^ n = cos(n * z) + 𝗂 * sin(n * z)"
  by (metis exp_Euler [symmetric] exp_of_nat_mult mult.left_commute)

Theorem (Euler's Formula for Complex Exponentials):
For any complex number \(z\), the exponential function \(e^z\) can be expressed as the product of a real part, \(e^{\text{Re}(z)}\), and a complex part, \((\cos(\text{Im}(z)) + i\sin(\text{Im}(z)))\), where \(i\) is the imaginary unit.

theorem Euler: "exp(z) = of_real(exp(Re z)) *
              (of_real(cos(Im z)) + 𝗂 * of_real(sin(Im z)))"
  by (simp add: Complex_eq cis.code exp_eq_polar)

Theorem (Sine of a Real Multiple of an Angle in Complex Exponential Form):
For a real number \(n\) and an angle \(a\), the sine of \(n\) times \(a\) is equal to the imaginary part of \((\text{cis } a)^n\), that is, \(\sin(n \cdot a) = \text{Im}((\text{cis } a)^n)\).

lemma sin_n_Im_cis_pow_n: "sin (real n * a) = Im (cis a ^ n)"
  by (auto simp add: DeMoivre)

Theorem (Fourier Series Exponential Identity):
For any natural number \(n\) and angle \(a\), the nth power of the sum of the cosine and sine functions, each multiplied by a constant, equals the sum of the cosine of \(n\) times \(a\) and the sine of \(n\) times \(a\), each multiplied by the same constant.

lemma fps_demoivre:
  "(fps_cos a + fps_const 𝗂 * fps_sin a)^n =
    fps_cos (of_nat n * a) + fps_const 𝗂 * fps_sin (of_nat n * a)"
  unfolding fps_exp_ii_sin_cos[symmetric] fps_exp_power_mult
  by (simp add: ac_simps)

Theorem (Fourier Series Representation of sine and cosine):
The Fourier sine and cosine series of a function can be expressed as \(f(\omega) = f_{sin}(\omega) \cdot \sin(\omega) - \omega \cdot f_{const} \cdot \cos(\omega)\), where \(f_{sin}\) and \(f_{const}\) are the Fourier sine and constant terms, respectively.

lemma fps_exp_minus_ii_sin_cos: "fps_exp (- (𝗂 * c)) = fps_cos c - fps_const 𝗂 * fps_sin c"
  unfolding minus_mult_right fps_exp_ii_sin_cos by (simp add: fps_sin_even fps_cos_odd)

Theorem (Fourier Series Sine and Cosine Representation):
Given a constant 𝗂 and a function c, the Fourier sine and cosine series of c can be expressed as the sum of a constant term and the product of 𝗂 with the sine and cosine functions of c, respectively: \(fps\_exp(\mathcal{O} \cdot c) = fps\_const(\mathcal{O}) \cdot fps\_sin(c) + \mathcal{O} \cdot fps\_cos(c)\).

lemma fps_exp_ii_sin_cos: "fps_exp (𝗂 * c) = fps_cos c + fps_const 𝗂 * fps_sin c"
  (is "?l = ?r")
proof -
  have "?l $ n = ?r $ n" for n
  proof (cases "even n")
    case True
    then obtain m where m: "n = 2 * m" ..
    show ?thesis
      by (simp add: m fps_sin_def fps_cos_def power_mult_distrib power_mult power_minus [of "c ^ 2"])
  next
    case False
    then obtain m where m: "n = 2 * m + 1" ..
    show ?thesis
      by (simp add: m fps_sin_def fps_cos_def power_mult_distrib
        power_mult power_minus [of "c ^ 2"])
  qed
  then show ?thesis
    by (simp add: fps_eq_iff)
qed

DeMoivre's Theorem states that for any real number \(a\) and integer \(n\), the complex number raised to the power \(n\) is given by \((cis(a))^n = cis(n \cdot a)\).

  by (auto simp add: DeMoivre)

Theorem (Sine of a Real Multiple of an Angle in Complex Exponential Form):
For a real number \(n\) and an angle \(a\), the sine of \(n\) times \(a\) is equal to the imaginary part of \((\text{cis } a)^n\), that is, \(\sin(n \cdot a) = \text{Im}((\text{cis } a)^n)\).

lemma sin_n_Im_cis_pow_n: "sin (real n * a) = Im (cis a ^ n)"
  by (auto simp add: DeMoivre)

Theorem (DeMoivre's Theorem for Complex Numbers):
For any complex number \(z\) and integer \(n\), the expression \((\cos(z) + \operatorname{i}\sin(z))^n\) simplifies to \(\cos(nz) + \operatorname{i}\sin(nz)\).

lemma DeMoivre: "(cos z + 𝗂 * sin z) ^ n = cos(n * z) + 𝗂 * sin(n * z)"
  by (metis exp_Euler [symmetric] exp_of_nat_mult mult.left_commute)

Theorem (Equivalence of Complex Numbers in Terms of Angles):
Given two complex numbers \(a\) and \(b\) such that their complex exponentials are equal (\(cis a = cis b\)), there exists an integer \(k\) for which the difference between \(a\) and \(b\) is equal to \(2\pi k\). This reflects the fact that complex numbers can be represented by angles in the complex plane, and their equivalence corresponds to a full rotation by \(2\pi\) radians.

lemma cis_eq:
  assumes "cis a = cis b"
  shows "∃ k::int. a - b = 2 * k * pi"
  using assms sin_cos_eq[of a b]
  using cis.sel[of a] cis.sel[of b]
  by (cases "cis a", cases "cis b") auto

Theorem (Cosine Equivalence):
For any complex number \(z\), the cosine of \(z\) equals 1 if and only if \(z\) can be expressed as \(2n\pi\), where \(n\) is an integer.

lemma cos_eq_1:
  fixes z::complex
  shows "cos z = 1 ⟷ (∃n::int. z = complex_of_real(2 * n * pi))"
  by (metis Re_complex_of_real cos_of_real cos_one_2pi_int cos_one_sin_zero mult.commute of_real_1 sin_eq_0)

Theorem (Cosine in Terms of Exponential Functions):
The cosine of a complex number \(z\) can be expressed as the average of the exponential function with \(z\) and its negation, specifically \(\cos(z) = \frac{e^{\mathrm{i}z} + e^{-\mathrm{i}z}}{2}\), where \(e\) is the base of the natural logarithm and \(\mathrm{i}\) is the imaginary unit.

lemma cos_exp_eq:  "cos z = (exp(𝗂 * z) + exp(-(𝗂 * z))) / 2"
  by (simp add: exp_Euler exp_minus_Euler)

Theorem (Euler's Formula for Complex Exponentials):
For any complex number \(z\), the exponential function \(e^z\) can be expressed as the product of a real part, \(e^{\text{Re}(z)}\), and a complex part, \((\cos(\text{Im}(z)) + i\sin(\text{Im}(z)))\), where \(i\) is the imaginary unit.

theorem Euler: "exp(z) = of_real(exp(Re z)) *
              (of_real(cos(Im z)) + 𝗂 * of_real(sin(Im z)))"
  by (simp add: Complex_eq cis.code exp_eq_polar)

Theorem (Cosine Equals Zero Implies Existence of Specific Angle):
Given a complex number \(z\), if the cosine of \(z\) is zero, then there exists an integer \(n\) such that \(z\) can be expressed as \(n \pi + \frac{\pi}{2}\), where \(n\) is an integer.

lemma cos_eq_0:
  fixes z::complex
  shows "cos z = 0 ⟷ (∃n::int. z = complex_of_real(n * pi) + of_real pi/2)"
  using sin_eq_0 [of "z - of_real pi/2"]
  by (simp add: sin_diff algebra_simps)

Theorem (Imaginary Part of Cosine):
The imaginary part of the cosine of a complex number \(z\) is given by \(\Im(\cos z) = \sin(\Re(z)) \cdot \frac{\exp(-i\Im(z)) - \exp(i\Im(z))}{2}\).

lemma Im_cos: "Im(cos z) = sin(Re z) * (exp(-(Im z)) - exp(Im z)) / 2"
  by (simp add: cos_exp_eq field_simps Im_divide Im_exp)

Theorem (Norm of Cosine Squared):
For any complex number \(z\), the square of the norm of the cosine function is equal to the square of the real part of \(z\) plus one-fourth the square of the difference between the exponential of the imaginary part of \(z\) and its inverse. Mathematically, this is expressed as \(\|\cos(z)\|^2 = \cos(\text{Re } z)^2 + \frac{(\exp(\text{Im } z) - \exp(-\text{Im } z))^2}{4}\).

lemma norm_cos_squared:
  "norm(cos z) ^ 2 = cos(Re z) ^ 2 + (exp(Im z) - inverse(exp(Im z))) ^ 2 / 4"
proof (cases z)
  case (Complex x1 x2)
  then show ?thesis
    apply (simp only: cos_add cmod_power2 cos_of_real sin_of_real Complex_eq)
    apply (simp add: cos_exp_eq sin_exp_eq exp_minus exp_of_real Re_divide Im_divide power_divide)
    apply (simp only: left_diff_distrib [symmetric] power_mult_distrib sin_squared_eq)
    apply (simp add: power2_eq_square field_split_simps)
    done
qed
