  assumes "n = length vts"
  assumes "l = x' - (∑i ∈ {1..n-2}. 1/(2^i))"
  assumes "x = l * (2^(n-3))"
  shows "x ∈ {0..1/2}"
        "p' x' = p x"     
proof-
  let ?f = "(λx::real. (x - (∑i ∈ {1..n-2}. 1/(2^i))) * (2^(n-2)))"
  have n_geq_4: "n ≥ 4" using polygon_vertices_length_at_least_4 assms 
    using polygon_of_def by blast
  moreover then have same_len: "length vts = length ?vts'"
    using assms rotate_polygon_vertices_same_length by auto
  moreover have length_vts': "length ?vts' = n" 
    using assms(4) same_len by auto
  ultimately have p'x': "p' x' = (linepath (?vts' ! (n-2)) (?vts' ! (n-1))) (?f x')"
    using polygon_linepath_images3[of n ?vts' p' x' ?f] assms
    unfolding polygon_of_def by fastforce

  have x_is: "x = (x' - (∑i = 1..n - 2. 1 / 2 ^ i)) * 2 ^ (n - 3)"
    using assms(5-6) by auto
  then  have x_gt: "x ≥ 0"
    using assms(3) by simp
  have sum_prop: "k ≥ 1 ⟹ 1 - (∑i = 1..k. 1 / (2 ^ i::real)) = 1/(2^k)" for k
  proof (induct k)
    case 0
    then show ?case by auto
  next
    case (Suc k)
    { assume * :"Suc k = 1"
      then have ?case by auto
    } moreover
    { assume *: "Suc k > 1"
      then have " 1 - (∑i = 1..k. 1 / (2 ^ i::real)) = 1 / 2 ^ k"
        using Suc by linarith
      then have ?case by simp
    }
    ultimately show ?case
      by linarith 
  qed
  have "x' ≤ 1"
    using assms(3) by auto
  then have "x ≤ (1 - (∑i = 1..n - 2. 1 / (2 ^ i::real))) * 2 ^ (n - 3)"
    using x_is 
    using mult_right_mono zero_le_power by fastforce
  then have "x ≤ 1/(2^(n-2))*2^(n-3)"
    using sum_prop n_geq_4 
    by auto
  then have x_lt: "x ≤ 1/2"
    using n_geq_4 
    by (smt (verit, ccfv_SIG) One_nat_def Suc_1 Suc_diff_Suc add_diff_cancel_right' diff_is_0_eq dual_order.trans linorder_not_le nonzero_mult_divide_mult_cancel_right2 numeral_3_eq_3 numeral_code(2) power.simps(2) power_commutes power_not_zero times_divide_eq_left zero_neq_numeral)
  then show "x ∈ {0..1/2}" 
    using x_gt x_lt by auto
  moreover have "n ≥ 3" using n_geq_4 by auto
  ultimately have px: "p x = (linepath (vts ! 0) (vts ! 1)) (2 * x)"
    using polygon_linepath_images1[of n vts] assms unfolding polygon_of_def by blast

  have "?vts' ! (n-2) = vts ! 0 ∧ ?vts' ! (n-1) = vts ! 1"
    unfolding rotate_polygon_vertices_def
    by (metis length_vts' assms(1) polygon_of_def rotate_polygon_vertices_def rotated_polygon_vertices_helper(1) rotated_polygon_vertices_helper(2))
  moreover have "?f x' = 2 * x"
  proof-
    have "2 * x = 2 * (x' - (∑i ∈ {1..n-2}. 1/(2^i))) * (2^(n-3))" using assms by auto
    moreover have "... = (x' - (∑i ∈ {1..n-2}. 1/(2^i))) * (2^(n-2))"
      using n_geq_4 Suc_1 Suc_diff_Suc Suc_le_eq bot_nat_0.not_eq_extremum diff_Suc_1 le_antisym mult.left_commute mult.right_neutral mult_cancel_left not_less_eq_eq num_double numeral_3_eq_3 numeral_eq_Suc numeral_times_numeral power.simps(2) pred_numeral_simps(2) zero_less_diff zero_neq_numeral
    proof -
      have f1: "∀r ra. (ra::real) * r = r * ra"
        by simp
      have f2: "∀r n ra. (r::real) * (r ^ n * ra) = r ^ Suc n * ra"
        by simp
      have f3: "pred_numeral (num.Bit1 num.One) = Suc (Suc 0)"
        by simp
      have f4: "Suc 0 = 1"
        by linarith
      have "Suc 1 < n"
        using n_geq_4 by linarith
      then have "2 * ((x' - (∑n = 1..n - Suc 1. 1 / 2 ^ n)) * 2 ^ (n - 3)) = (x' - (∑n = 1..n - Suc 1. 1 / 2 ^ n)) * 2 ^ (n - Suc 1)"
        using f4 f3 f2 f1 Suc_diff_Suc numeral_eq_Suc by presburger
      then show ?thesis
        by (metis (no_types) Suc_1 mult.assoc)
    qed
    moreover have "... = ?f x'" by auto
    ultimately show ?thesis by presburger
  qed
  ultimately show "p' x' = p x" using p'x' px by auto
qed

Title query.refined_query: Theorem (Probability of Shared Birthdays): Given that there are no leap years, the probability that at least two people in a group share the same birthday is significantly higher than one might initially assume. This counterintuitive result demonstrates how combinatorial probabilities can defy common expectations when dealing with large sample sizes.

Theorem (Birthday Paradox for Function Sets):
Given a set S with 23 elements and a set T with 365 elements, the birthday paradox states that at least twice the number of elements in S (i.e., 2 * |S|) is greater than or equal to the number of distinct functions from S to T (i.e., |extensional_funcset(S, T)|), where each function is not injective (i.e., ¬ inj_on).

lemma birthday_paradox:
  assumes "card S = 23" "card T = 365"
  shows "2 * card {f ∈ extensional_funcset S T. ¬ inj_on f S} ≥ card (extensional_funcset S T)"
proof -
  from ‹card S = 23› ‹card T = 365› have "finite S" "finite T" "card S ≤ card T"
    by (auto intro: card_ge_0_finite)
  from assms show ?thesis
    using card_PiE[OF ‹finite S›, of "λi. T"] ‹finite S›
      card_extensional_funcset_not_inj_on[OF ‹finite S› ‹finite T› ‹card S ≤ card T›]
    by (simp add: fact_div_fact prod_upto_nat_unfold prod_constant)
qed

Theorem (Sum of Probabilities in a Probability Space):
Given a probability space with events P and Q, if for all n, the nth probability P n is an event and Q is an event, and there exists a unique n such that P n implies Q, then the probability of the sum of events P n is equal to the probability of event Q.

lemma (in prob_space) prob_sums:
  assumes P: "⋀n. {x∈space M. P n x} ∈ events"
  assumes Q: "{x∈space M. Q x} ∈ events"
  assumes ae: "AE x in M. (∀n. P n x ⟶ Q x) ∧ (Q x ⟶ (∃!n. P n x))"
  shows "(λn. 𝒫(x in M. P n x)) sums 𝒫(x in M. Q x)"
proof -
  from ae[THEN AE_E_prob] obtain S
    where S:
      "S ⊆ {x ∈ space M. (∀n. P n x ⟶ Q x) ∧ (Q x ⟶ (∃!n. P n x))}"
      "S ∈ events"
      "prob S = 1"
    by auto
  then have disj: "disjoint_family (λn. {x∈space M. P n x} ∩ S)"
    by (auto simp: disjoint_family_on_def)
  from S have ae_S:
    "AE x in M. x ∈ {x∈space M. Q x} ⟷ x ∈ (⋃n. {x∈space M. P n x} ∩ S)"
    "⋀n. AE x in M. x ∈ {x∈space M. P n x} ⟷ x ∈ {x∈space M. P n x} ∩ S"
    using ae by (auto dest!: AE_prob_1)
  from ae_S have *:
    "𝒫(x in M. Q x) = prob (⋃n. {x∈space M. P n x} ∩ S)"
    using P Q S by (intro finite_measure_eq_AE) auto
  from ae_S have **:
    "⋀n. 𝒫(x in M. P n x) = prob ({x∈space M. P n x} ∩ S)"
    using P Q S by (intro finite_measure_eq_AE) auto
  show ?thesis
    unfolding * ** using S P disj
    by (intro finite_measure_UNION) auto
qed

Theorem (Sum of Probabilities in a Probability Space):
Given a finite index set \(I\) and two events \(P\) and \(Q\) in a probability space \(M\), if \(P\) is defined for all \(n \in I\) and \(Q\) is an event, and there exists a unique \(n \in I\) such that \(P n\) implies \(Q\), then the probability of \(Q\) is equal to the sum of the probabilities of \(P n\) for all \(n \in I\). Mathematically, this is expressed as \(\Pr(Q) = \sum_{n \in I} \Pr(P n)\).

lemma (in prob_space) prob_sum:
  assumes [simp, intro]: "finite I"
  assumes P: "⋀n. n ∈ I ⟹ {x∈space M. P n x} ∈ events"
  assumes Q: "{x∈space M. Q x} ∈ events"
  assumes ae: "AE x in M. (∀n∈I. P n x ⟶ Q x) ∧ (Q x ⟶ (∃!n∈I. P n x))"
  shows "𝒫(x in M. Q x) = (∑n∈I. 𝒫(x in M. P n x))"
proof -
  from ae[THEN AE_E_prob] obtain S
    where S:
      "S ⊆ {x ∈ space M. (∀n∈I. P n x ⟶ Q x) ∧ (Q x ⟶ (∃!n. n ∈ I ∧ P n x))}"
      "S ∈ events"
      "prob S = 1"
    by auto
  then have disj: "disjoint_family_on (λn. {x∈space M. P n x} ∩ S) I"
    by (auto simp: disjoint_family_on_def)
  from S have ae_S:
    "AE x in M. x ∈ {x∈space M. Q x} ⟷ x ∈ (⋃n∈I. {x∈space M. P n x} ∩ S)"
    "⋀n. n ∈ I ⟹ AE x in M. x ∈ {x∈space M. P n x} ⟷ x ∈ {x∈space M. P n x} ∩ S"
    using ae by (auto dest!: AE_prob_1)
  from ae_S have *:
    "𝒫(x in M. Q x) = prob (⋃n∈I. {x∈space M. P n x} ∩ S)"
    using P Q S by (intro finite_measure_eq_AE) (auto intro!: sets.Int)
  from ae_S have **:
    "⋀n. n ∈ I ⟹ 𝒫(x in M. P n x) = prob ({x∈space M. P n x} ∩ S)"
    using P Q S by (intro finite_measure_eq_AE) auto
  show ?thesis
    using S P disj
    by (auto simp add: * ** simp del: UN_simps intro!: finite_measure_finite_Union)
qed

Theorem (Sum of Probabilities with Replication):
For any natural number \(n\) and a probability space defined by \(\Phi\), the sum of the probabilities of events \(\phi\) in \(\Phi\) replicated \(n\) times is equal to the sum of the probabilities of the original events \(\phi\) in \(\Phi\), each replicated \(n\) times. Formally, \(\sum_{\phi \in \Phi} \mathbb{P}(\phi) + n = \sum_{\phi \in \text{rep}(n, \Phi)} \mathbb{P}(\phi)\), where \(\text{rep}(n, \Phi)\) denotes the set of all events obtained by replicating each event in \(\Phi\) \(n\) times.

lemma (in probability_logic) probability_replicate_verum:
  fixes n :: nat
  shows "(∑φ←Φ. 𝒫 φ) + n = (∑φ←(replicate n ⊤) @ Φ. 𝒫 φ)"
  using probability_unity
  by (induct n, auto)

Theorem (Probability of Sample Geometric Distribution):
Given a geometric distribution with parameter \(n\), the probability that a randomly selected sample is less than or equal to \(2^j\) is bounded by \(1/2^j\), formally expressed as \(\text{measure}(\text{sample\_pro}(\text{geom\_pro}(n))) \leq 1/2^j\).

This theorem relates to the study of universal hash families, where geometric distributions are used to analyze the performance and security of cryptographic hash functions and randomized algorithms in data structures. It quantifies the likelihood of outcomes within a geometric probability space, ensuring that the distribution of sample points adheres to a specific probabilistic constraint.

lemma geom_pro_prob_single:
  "measure (sample_pro (geom_pro n)) {j} ≤ 1 / 2^j" (is "?L ≤ ?R")
proof -
  have "?L = measure (sample_pro (geom_pro n)) ({j..}-{j+1..})"
    by (intro measure_pmf_cong) auto
  also have "... = measure (sample_pro (geom_pro n)) {j..} - measure (sample_pro (geom_pro n)) {j+1..}"
    by (intro measure_Diff) auto
  also have "... = measure (sample_pro (geom_pro n)) {ω. ω ≥ j}-measure (sample_pro (geom_pro n)) {ω. ω ≥ (j+1)}"
    by (intro arg_cong2[where f="(-)"] measure_pmf_cong) auto
  also have "... = of_bool (j ≤ n) * 1 / 2 ^ j - of_bool (j + 1 ≤ n) / 2 ^ (j + 1)"
    unfolding geom_pro_prob by simp
  also have "... ≤ 1/2^j - 0"
    by (intro diff_mono) auto
  also have "... = ?R" by simp
  finally show ?thesis by simp
qed

Theorem (Natural Number Probability):
Given a natural number \(n > 0\), the probability mass function (pmf) of a random variable defined by the lemma is equal to the pmf of a set with elements less than \(n\).

lemma nat_pro:
  assumes "n > 0"
  shows "sample_pro (nat_pro n) = pmf_of_set {..<n}"
  unfolding sample_pro_alt nat_pro_size[OF assms] by (simp add:nat_pro_def)

Theorem (Probability of Intersection of Events):
Given a non-empty list of events `xs` and a subset `S` of these events with positive probability, the probability of the intersection of `S` with the union of all subsets of `xs` is equal to the product of the probabilities of each individual subset of `xs` within `S`. Formally, if `xs` is a non-empty list of events, `S` is a non-empty subset of `xs` with positive probability, and `S` is finite, then:

\[
\Pr(\bigcap_{s \in S} s) = \prod_{i=0}^{\text{length}(xs)-1} \Pr((xs ! i) \cap (\bigcup_{s \in S} s))
\]

This theorem formalizes the relationship between the probability of a collective event and the product of individual event probabilities within a structured subset, using the probabilistic method in combinatorics.

lemma prob_cond_Inter_take_cond:
  assumes "xs ≠ []"
  assumes "set xs ⊆ events"
  assumes "S ⊆ events"
  assumes "S ≠ {}"
  assumes "finite S"
  assumes "prob (⋂S) > 0"
  shows "𝒫((⋂(set xs)) | (⋂ S)) = (∏i = 0..<(length xs) .  𝒫((xs ! i) | (⋂(set (take i xs ) ∪ S))))"
proof -
  define M' where "M' = uniform_measure M (⋂S)"
  interpret cps: prob_space M' using prob_space_cond_prob_event M'_def assms(6) by auto
  have len: "length xs > 0" using assms(1) by simp
  have cps_ev: "cps.events = events" using sets_uniform_measure M'_def by auto
  have sevents: "⋂S ∈ events" using assms(3) assms(4) Inter_event_ss assms(5) by auto
  have fin: "finite (set xs)" by auto
  then have xevents: "⋂(set xs) ∈ events" using assms(1) assms(2) Inter_event_ss by blast
  then have peq: "𝒫((⋂(set xs)) | (⋂ S)) = cps.prob (⋂ (set xs))" 
    using measure_uniform_measure_eq_cond_prob_ev3[of "⋂(set xs)" "⋂S"] sevents M'_def
    by blast
  then have "cps.prob (⋂ (set xs)) = cps.prob (hd xs) * (∏i = 1..<(length xs) . 
    cps.cond_prob_ev (xs ! i) (⋂(set (take i xs ))))" using assms cps.prob_cond_Inter_List cps_ev 
    by blast
  moreover have "cps.prob (hd xs) = 𝒫((xs ! 0) | (⋂(set (take 0 xs ) ∪ S)))"
  proof -
    have ev: "hd xs ∈ events" using assms(2) len by auto
    then have "cps.prob (hd xs) = 𝒫(hd xs | ⋂S)" 
      using ev sevents measure_uniform_measure_eq_cond_prob_ev3[of "hd xs" "⋂S"] M'_def by presburger
    then show ?thesis using len by (simp add: hd_conv_nth)
  qed
  moreover have "⋀i. i > 0 ⟹ i < length xs ⟹ 
    cps.cond_prob_ev (xs ! i) (⋂(set (take i xs ))) = 𝒫((xs ! i) | (⋂(set (take i xs ) ∪ S)))"
  proof -
    fix i assume igt: "i > 0" and ilt: "i <length xs"
    then have "set (take i xs) ⊆ events" using assms(2)
      by (meson set_take_subset subset_trans) 
    moreover have "set (take i xs) ≠ {}" using len igt ilt by auto
    ultimately have "(⋂(set (take i xs ))) ∈ events"
      using Inter_event_ss fin by auto
    moreover have "xs ! i ∈ events" using assms(2)
      using nth_mem subset_iff igt ilt by blast
    moreover have "(⋂(set (take i xs ) ∪ S)) = (⋂(set (take i xs ))) ∩ (⋂S)"
      by (simp add: Inf_union_distrib) 
    ultimately show "cps.cond_prob_ev (xs ! i) (⋂(set (take i xs ))) = 𝒫((xs ! i) | (⋂(set (take i xs ) ∪ S)))"
      using sevents cond_prob_ev_double[of "xs ! i" "(⋂(set (take i xs )))" "⋂S"] assms(6) M'_def by presburger 
  qed
  ultimately have eq: "cps.prob (⋂ (set xs)) = 𝒫((xs ! 0) | (⋂(set (take 0 xs ) ∪ S))) * (∏i ∈ {1..<(length xs)} . 
    𝒫((xs ! i) | (⋂(set (take i xs ) ∪ S))))" by simp
  moreover have "{1..<length xs} = {0..<length xs} - {0}"
    by (simp add: atLeast1_lessThan_eq_remove0 lessThan_atLeast0)
  moreover have "finite {0..<length xs}" by auto
  moreover have "0 ∈ {0..<length xs}"by (simp add: assms(1)) 
  ultimately have "𝒫((xs ! 0) | (⋂(set (take 0 xs ) ∪ S))) * (∏i ∈ {1..<(length xs)} . 
    𝒫((xs ! i) | (⋂(set (take i xs ) ∪ S)))) = (∏i ∈ {0..<(length xs)} . 
    𝒫((xs ! i) | (⋂(set (take i xs ) ∪ S))))" using prod.remove[of "{0..<length xs}" "0" "λ i. 𝒫((xs ! i) | (⋂(set (take i xs ) ∪ S)))"]
    by presburger
  then have "cps.prob (⋂ (set xs)) = (∏i ∈ {0..<(length xs)} . 
    𝒫((xs ! i) | (⋂(set (take i xs ) ∪ S))))" using eq by simp
  then show ?thesis using peq by auto
qed

Theorem (Probability of Two Coins Tossing True):
Given a classical list update problem, the probability of both coins landing on 'True' is 0.7, as derived from the pmf (probability mass function) of the 'twocoins' event.

unfolding twocoins_def

Theorem (Distributed Cardinality Estimation):
Given a set \( t \) of sketches with cardinality less than \( n \), and a real number \( X \) representing the actual size of \( t \), we define a probability mass function \( p \) for the set of elements up to a certain threshold \( \Theta \). The theorem establishes that the measure of the set of elements whose estimated value, when evaluated at \( t \), deviates from \( X \) by more than \( \epsilon \cdot X \), is bounded by \( \delta \). Formally, \( \mu(p \cap \{ \omega : |eval(\omega, t) - X| > \epsilon \cdot X \}) \leq \delta \).

theorem correctness:
  fixes X
  assumes "sketch_tree_set t ⊆ {..<n}"
  defines "p ≡ pmf_of_set {..<pro_size Θ}"
  defines "X ≡ real (card (sketch_tree_set t))"
  shows "measure p {ω. ¦estimate (eval ω t) - X¦ > ε * X} ≤ δ" (is "?L ≤ ?R")
proof -
  define A where "A = sketch_tree_set t"
  have X_eq: "X = real (card A)"
    unfolding X_def A_def by simp

  have 0:"eval ω t = ν ω A" for ω
    unfolding A_def using single_result merge_result
    by (induction t) (auto simp del:merge.simps single.simps)

  have 1: "A ⊆ {..<n}"
    using assms(1) unfolding A_def by blast

  have 2: "A ≠ {}"
    unfolding A_def by (induction t) auto

  show ?thesis
    unfolding 0 X_eq p_def by (intro estimate_result 1 2)
qed

Theorem (Approximate Model Counting Probability):
Given a countable collection of sets \(A\) with a probability measure \(M\) and a countable family of sets \(B_i\) with a probability measure \(N\), if for each element \(a\) in \(A\) the probability of \(B_i\) under \(N\) equals a constant \(r\), then the probability of the pairwise intersection of \(A\) and \(B_i\) under \(M\) is the product of the probability measure of \(A\) under \(M\) and the constant \(r\).

lemma measure_pmf_prob_dependent_product_bound_eq':
  assumes "countable (A ∩ set_pmf M)" "⋀i. countable (B i ∩ set_pmf N)"
  assumes "⋀a. a ∈ A ∩ set_pmf M ⟹ measure_pmf.prob N (B a ∩ set_pmf N) = r"
  shows "measure_pmf.prob (pair_pmf M N) (Sigma A B) = measure_pmf.prob M A * r"
proof -
  have *: "Sigma A B ∩ (set_pmf M × set_pmf N) =
    Sigma (A ∩ set_pmf M) (λi. B i ∩ set_pmf N)"
    by auto

  have "measure_pmf.prob (pair_pmf M N) (Sigma A B) =
    measure_pmf.prob (pair_pmf M N) (Sigma (A ∩ set_pmf M) (λi. B i ∩ set_pmf N))"
    by (metis * measure_Int_set_pmf set_pair_pmf)
  moreover have "... =
    measure_pmf.prob M (A ∩ set_pmf M) * r"
    using measure_pmf_prob_dependent_product_bound_eq[OF assms(1-3)]
    by auto
  moreover have "... = measure_pmf.prob M A * r"
    by (simp add: measure_Int_set_pmf)
  ultimately show ?thesis by linarith
qed

Theorem (Collision Probability in Hashing):
Given a set \(A\) and a constant \(c \geq 1\), the probability of finding at least one pair \((x, y)\) in \(A\) such that \(x \neq y\), \(x\) and \(y\) have the same hash value, and the hash value is less than or equal to \(c\), is bounded above by \((5/2) \cdot (\text{card}(A))^{2} \cdot c^{2} \cdot 2^{-\text{real}(r)} / (\text{real}(p))^{2} + 1/\text{real}(p)\).

private lemma collision_prob:
  assumes "c ≥ 1"
  shows "prob {ω. ∃x ∈ set as. ∃y ∈ set as. x ≠ y ∧ tr_hash x ω ≤ c ∧ tr_hash x ω = tr_hash y ω} ≤
    (5/2) * (real (card (set as)))⇧2 * c⇧2 * 2 powr -(real r) / (real p)⇧2 + 1/real p" (is "prob {ω. ?l ω} ≤ ?r1 + ?r2")
proof -
  define ρ :: real where "ρ = 9/8"

  have rho_c_ge_0: "ρ * c ≥ 0" unfolding ρ_def using assms by simp

  have c_ge_0: "c≥0" using assms by simp

  have "degree ω ≥ 1 ⟹ ω ∈ space ⟹ degree ω = 1" for ω
    by (simp add:bounded_degree_polynomials_def space_def)
     (metis One_nat_def Suc_1 le_less_Suc_eq less_imp_diff_less list.size(3) pos2)

  hence a: "⋀ω x y. x < p ⟹ y < p ⟹  x ≠ y ⟹ degree ω ≥ 1 ⟹ ω ∈ space ⟹  hash x ω ≠ hash y ω"
    using inj_onD[OF inj_if_degree_1]  mod_ring_carr by blast

  have b: "prob {ω. degree ω ≥ 1 ∧ tr_hash x ω ≤ c ∧ tr_hash x ω = tr_hash y ω} ≤ 5 * c⇧2 * 2 powr (-real r) /(real p)⇧2"
    if b_assms: "x ∈ set as"  "y ∈ set as"  "x < y" for x y
  proof -
    have c: "real u ≤ ρ * c ∧ ¦real u - real v¦ ≤ ρ * c * 2 powr (-real r)"

Theorem (Probability of Hash Collision):
Given a universal hash family where \(x\) is an element of the set \(R\), the probability that a randomly chosen hash \(h(x)\) matches a specific hash \(ω\) in set \(A\) is equal to the ratio of the intersection cardinality of \(A\) and \(R\) to the size of the field, expressed as \(\Pr[\text{hash } x = ω] = \frac{|A \cap R|}{\text{field size}}\).

lemma prob_range:
  assumes [simp]:"x ∈ carrier R"
  shows "prob {ω. hash x ω ∈ A} = card (A ∩ carrier R) / field_size"
proof -
  have "prob {ω. hash x ω ∈ A} = prob (⋃a ∈ A ∩ carrier R. {ω. hash x ω = a})"
    by (rule measure_pmf_eq, auto simp:M_def)
  also have "... = (∑ a ∈ (A ∩ carrier R). prob {ω. hash x ω = a})"
    by (rule measure_finite_Union, auto simp:M_def disjoint_family_on_def)
  also have "... = (∑ a ∈ (A ∩ carrier R). 1/(real field_size))"
    by (rule sum.cong, auto simp:prob_single)
  also have "... = card (A ∩ carrier R) / field_size"
    by simp
  finally show ?thesis by simp
qed

Theorem (Probability of Intersection Bounds):
Given a finite set A and subsets B and C where B is non-empty and B is a subset of A, the probability of the intersection of all events in B is less than or equal to the probability of the intersection of all events in C. This is formalized as \( P(\bigcap_{F \in F} F \subseteq A) \leq P(\bigcap_{F \in F} F \subseteq B) \), assuming B is not empty and B is contained within A.

lemma prob_inter_ss_lt_index: 
  assumes "finite A"
  assumes "F ` A ⊆ events"
  assumes "B ≠ {}"
  assumes "B ⊆ A"
  shows "prob (⋂(F ` A)) ≤ prob (⋂(F `B))"
using prob_inter_ss_lt[of "F ` A" "F ` B"] assms by auto

Theorem (Probability of Intersection of Events):
Given a non-empty set \( S \) of events within a probability space, and assuming \( S \) has a finite number of elements, the probability of the intersection of all events in \( S \) is equal to the probability of the first event in \( S \) multiplied by the product of the probabilities of each event in \( S \) taken one by one. Formally, \( P(\bigcap S) = P(\text{head}(S)) \times \prod_{i=1}^{\text{length}(S)} P(\text{take}(i, S)) \).

lemma prob_cond_Inter_take: 
  assumes " S ≠ {}"
  assumes "S ⊆ events"
  assumes "finite S"
  obtains xs where "set xs = S" and "length xs = card S" and 
    "prob (⋂S) = prob (hd xs) * (∏i = 1..<(length xs) . 𝒫((xs ! i) | (⋂(set (take i xs )))))"
  using assms prob_cond_Inter_List exists_list_card 
  by (metis (no_types, lifting) set_empty2 subset_code(1))

Theorem (Conditional Probability of Intersection):
Given two events A and B within a sample space M, the probability of B given A is the ratio of the probability that both A and B occur to the probability of A occurring alone. Mathematically, this is expressed as \( P(B | A) = \frac{P(\omega \in B \cap A)}{P(\omega \in A)} \).

lemma cond_prob_inter: "𝒫(B | A) = 𝒫(ω in M. (ω ∈ B ∩ A)) / 𝒫(ω in M. (ω ∈ A))"
  using cond_prob_def by auto

Theorem (Independence in Universal Hash Families):
Given a universal hash family, where each hash function is independent, the probability of two distinct inputs being mapped to the same output (collision) is extremely low, specifically \(p = 1 / 2^{j}\), where \(j\) is the number of bits in the hash output.

private lemma p_prime : "prime p" and j_gt_0: "j > 0"
proof -
  obtain q r where 0:"pro_size S = q^r" and q_prime: "prime q" and r_gt_0: "r > 0"
    using size_prime_power is_prime_power_def by blast

  have "(p,j) = split_power (q^r)" unfolding split_power 0 by simp
  also have "... = (q,r)" by (intro split_power_prime q_prime r_gt_0)
  finally have "(p,j) = (q,r)" by simp
  thus "prime p" "j > 0" using q_prime r_gt_0 by auto
qed

Theorem (Probability of Intersection of Events):
Given a finite set of events \(A\) that are all subsets of a larger set of events \(events\), with each event \(A_i\) satisfying \(0 \leq f_{A_i} \leq 1\), and the probability of each event \(A_i\) being at least \(f_{A_i}\), the probability of the intersection of all events in \(A\) is at least the product of the probabilities of each individual event, that is, \(P(\bigcap_{A_i \in A} A_i) \geq \prod_{a' \in A} f_{a'}\).

lemma prob_cond_Inter_set_bound: 
  assumes " A ≠ {}"
  assumes "A ⊆ events"
  assumes "finite A"
  assumes "⋀ Ai . f Ai ≥ 0 ∧ f Ai ≤ 1"
  assumes "⋀Ai S. Ai ∈ A ⟹ S ⊆ A - {Ai} ⟹ S ≠ {} ⟹ 𝒫(Ai | (⋂S)) ≥ f Ai"
  assumes "⋀ Ai. Ai ∈ A ⟹ prob Ai ≥ f Ai"
  shows "prob (⋂A) ≥ (∏a' ∈ A .  f a')"
proof - 
  obtain xs where eq: "set xs = A" and seq: "length xs = card A" and
    pA: "prob (⋂A) = prob (hd xs) * (∏i = 1..<(length xs) . 𝒫((xs ! i) | (⋂ j ∈ {0..<i} . xs ! j)))"
    using assms obtains_prob_cond_Inter_index[of A] by blast
  then have dis: "distinct xs" using card_distinct
    by metis 
  then have "hd xs ∈ A" using eq hd_in_set assms(1) by auto
  then have "prob (hd xs) ≥ (f (hd xs))" using assms(6) by blast
  have "⋀ i. i ∈ {1..<(length xs)} ⟹ 𝒫((xs ! i) | (⋂ j ∈ {0..<i} . xs ! j)) ≥ f (xs ! i)"
  proof -
    fix i assume "i ∈ {1..<length xs}"
    then have ilb: "i ≥ 1" and iub: "i < length xs" by auto
    then have xsin: "xs ! i ∈ A" using eq by auto
    define S where "S = (λ j. xs ! j) ` {0..<i}"
    then have "S = set (take i xs)"
      by (simp add: iub less_or_eq_imp_le nth_image)
    then have "xs ! i ∉ S" using dis set_take_distinct_elem_not iub by simp
    then have "S ⊆ A - {(xs ! i)}"
      using ‹S = set (take i xs)› eq set_take_subset by fastforce 
    moreover have "S ≠ {}" using S_def ilb by (simp) 
    moreover have "𝒫((xs ! i) | (⋂ j ∈ {0..<i} . xs ! j)) = 𝒫((xs ! i) | (⋂ Aj ∈ S . Aj))" 
      using S_def by auto
    ultimately show "𝒫((xs ! i) | (⋂ j ∈ {0..<i} . xs ! j)) ≥ f (xs ! i)"
      using assms(5) xsin by auto
  qed
  then have "(∏i = 1..<(length xs) . 𝒫((xs ! i) | (⋂ j ∈ {0..<i} . xs ! j))) ≥ 
    (∏i = 1..<(length xs) . f (xs ! i))"
    by (meson assms(4) prod_mono)
  moreover have "(∏i = 1..<(length xs) . f (xs ! i)) = (∏a ∈ A - {hd xs} . f a)"
  proof -
    have ne: "xs ≠ []" using assms(1) eq by auto
    have "A = (λ j. xs ! j) ` {0..<length xs}" using eq
      by (simp add: nth_image) 
    have "A - {hd xs} = set (tl xs) " using dis
      by (metis Diff_insert_absorb distinct.simps(2) eq list.exhaust_sel list.set(2) ne)
    also have "... = (λ j. xs ! j) ` {1..<length xs}" using nth_image_tl ne by auto
    finally have Ahdeq: "A - {hd xs} = (λ j. xs ! j) ` {1..<length xs}" by simp
    have io: "inj_on (nth xs) {1..<length xs}" using inj_on_nth dis
      by (metis atLeastLessThan_iff) 
    have "(∏i = 1..<(length xs) . f (xs ! i)) = (∏i ∈ {1..<(length xs)} . f (xs ! i))" by simp
    also have "... = (∏i ∈ (λ j. xs ! j) ` {1..<length xs} . f i)" 
      using io by (simp add: prod.reindex_cong) 
    finally show ?thesis using Ahdeq
      using ‹(∏i = 1..<length xs. f (xs ! i)) = prod f ((!) xs ` {1..<length xs})› by presburger 
  qed
  ultimately have "prob (⋂A) ≥ f (hd xs) * (∏a ∈ A - {hd xs} . f a)"
    using pA ‹f (hd xs) ≤ prob (hd xs)› assms(4) ordered_comm_semiring_class.comm_mult_left_mono
    by (simp add: mult_mono' prod_nonneg)  
  then show ?thesis
    by (metis ‹hd xs ∈ A› assms(3) prod.remove) 
qed

Theorem (Probability of Hash Collision for Uniform Hash Functions):
Given a finite field \(F\) and a non-zero element \(x\) in \(F\), for any positive integer \(n\), the probability that two random elements \(y_1\) and \(y_2\) from \(F\) hash to the same value under a uniform hash function is equal to the ratio of the number of elements in \(F\) to the cardinality of \(F\). Formally, the measure of the event where \(y_1\) and \(y_2\) hash to the same value \(y\) is \(\frac{|F|}{|F|}\), where \(|F|\) denotes the number of elements in the field \(F\).

lemma hash_prob_single':
  assumes "field F" "finite (carrier F)"
  assumes "x ∈ carrier F"
  assumes "1 ≤ n"
  shows "measure (pmf_of_set (bounded_degree_polynomials F n)) {ω. ring.hash F x ω = y} =
    of_bool (y∈ carrier F)/(real (card (carrier F)))" (is "?L = ?R")
proof (cases "y ∈ carrier F")
  case True
  have "?L = 𝒫(ω in pmf_of_set (bounded_degree_polynomials F n). ring.hash F x ω = y)" by simp
  also have "... = 1 / (real (card (carrier F)))" by (intro hash_prob_single assms conjI True)
  also have "... = ?R" using True by simp
  finally show ?thesis by simp
next
  case False
  interpret field "F" using assms by simp
  have fin_carr: "finite (carrier F)" using assms by simp
  note S = non_empty_bounded_degree_polynomials fin_degree_bounded[OF fin_carr]
  let ?S = "bounded_degree_polynomials F n"

  have "hash x f ≠ y" if "f ∈ ?S" for f
  proof -
    have "hash x f ∈ carrier F"
      using that unfolding hash_def bounded_degree_polynomials_def
      by (intro eval_in_carrier assms) (simp add: polynomial_incl univ_poly_carrier)
    thus ?thesis using False by auto
  qed
  hence "?L = measure (pmf_of_set (bounded_degree_polynomials F n)) {}"
    using S by (intro measure_eq_AE AE_pmfI) simp_all
  also have "... = ?R" using False by simp
  finally show ?thesis by simp
qed

Theorem (Probability of Intersection of Independent Events):
Given a collection of events \(A_i\) that are mutually independent, if \(J\) is a non-empty subset of these events, then the probability of the intersection of event \(A\) with the intersection of all events in \(J\) is equal to the product of the probability of \(A\) and the probability of the intersection of all events in \(J\). Formally, \(P(A \cap \bigcap_{j \in J} F_j) = P(A) \cdot \prod_{j \in J} P(F_j)\).

lemma mutual_indep_eventsD[dest]: "mutual_indep_events A F I ⟹ J ⊆ I ⟹ J ≠ {} ⟹ prob (A ∩ (⋂j ∈ J . F j)) = prob A * prob (⋂j ∈ J . F j)"
  using mutual_indep_events_def by simp

Theorem (Universal Hashing):
Given a universal hash family \(k\), for any two distinct keys \(x, y\) in the key space \(R\), the probability of a collision (i.e., \(k(x) = k(y)\)) is bounded above by \(1/|R|\), where \(|R|\) is the size of the key space. This property ensures that the hash functions are evenly distributed, which is crucial for the performance and security of hash-based algorithms in cryptography and data structures.

theorem k_universal:
  "k_universal k hash (carrier R) (carrier R)"
  using uniform k_wise_indep by (simp add:k_universal_def)

Theorem (Probability Function Equality under Differential Privacy):
Given a non-negative real number ε representing privacy loss, the probability of an event under differential privacy is such that \(1 - e^{-\epsilon} / (1 + e^{-\epsilon})\) is equal to \(1 / (1 + e^{-\epsilon})\).

Theorem (Sum of Probabilities in a Probability Space):
Given a probability space with events P and Q, if for all n, the nth probability P n is an event and Q is an event, and there exists a unique n such that P n implies Q, then the probability of the sum of events P n is equal to the probability of event Q.

lemma (in prob_space) prob_sums:
  assumes P: "⋀n. {x∈space M. P n x} ∈ events"
  assumes Q: "{x∈space M. Q x} ∈ events"
  assumes ae: "AE x in M. (∀n. P n x ⟶ Q x) ∧ (Q x ⟶ (∃!n. P n x))"
  shows "(λn. 𝒫(x in M. P n x)) sums 𝒫(x in M. Q x)"
proof -
  from ae[THEN AE_E_prob] obtain S
    where S:
      "S ⊆ {x ∈ space M. (∀n. P n x ⟶ Q x) ∧ (Q x ⟶ (∃!n. P n x))}"
      "S ∈ events"
      "prob S = 1"
    by auto
  then have disj: "disjoint_family (λn. {x∈space M. P n x} ∩ S)"
    by (auto simp: disjoint_family_on_def)
  from S have ae_S:
    "AE x in M. x ∈ {x∈space M. Q x} ⟷ x ∈ (⋃n. {x∈space M. P n x} ∩ S)"
    "⋀n. AE x in M. x ∈ {x∈space M. P n x} ⟷ x ∈ {x∈space M. P n x} ∩ S"
    using ae by (auto dest!: AE_prob_1)

    "𝒫(x in M. Q x) = prob (⋃n. {x∈space M. P n x} ∩ S)"
    using P Q S by (intro finite_measure_eq_AE) auto
  from ae_S have **:
    "⋀n. 𝒫(x in M. P n x) = prob ({x∈space M. P n x} ∩ S)"
    using P Q S by (intro finite_measure_eq_AE) auto
  show ?thesis
    unfolding * ** using S P disj
    by (intro finite_measure_UNION) auto

Theorem (Probability of Intersection of Events):
Given a finite set of events \(A\) that are all subsets of a larger set of events \(events\), with each event \(A_i\) satisfying \(0 \leq f_{A_i} \leq 1\), and the probability of each event \(A_i\) being at least \(f_{A_i}\), the probability of the intersection of all events in \(A\) is at least the product of the probabilities of each individual event, that is, \(P(\bigcap_{A_i \in A} A_i) \geq \prod_{a' \in A} f_{a'}\).

lemma prob_cond_Inter_set_bound: 
  assumes " A ≠ {}"
  assumes "A ⊆ events"
  assumes "finite A"
  assumes "⋀ Ai . f Ai ≥ 0 ∧ f Ai ≤ 1"
  assumes "⋀Ai S. Ai ∈ A ⟹ S ⊆ A - {Ai} ⟹ S ≠ {} ⟹ 𝒫(Ai | (⋂S)) ≥ f Ai"
  assumes "⋀ Ai. Ai ∈ A ⟹ prob Ai ≥ f Ai"
  shows "prob (⋂A) ≥ (∏a' ∈ A .  f a')"
proof - 
  obtain xs where eq: "set xs = A" and seq: "length xs = card A" and
    pA: "prob (⋂A) = prob (hd xs) * (∏i = 1..<(length xs) . 𝒫((xs ! i) | (⋂ j ∈ {0..<i} . xs ! j)))"
    using assms obtains_prob_cond_Inter_index[of A] by blast
  then have dis: "distinct xs" using card_distinct
    by metis 
  then have "hd xs ∈ A" using eq hd_in_set assms(1) by auto
  then have "prob (hd xs) ≥ (f (hd xs))" using assms(6) by blast
  have "⋀ i. i ∈ {1..<(length xs)} ⟹ 𝒫((xs ! i) | (⋂ j ∈ {0..<i} . xs ! j)) ≥ f (xs ! i)"
  proof -
    fix i assume "i ∈ {1..<length xs}"
    then have ilb: "i ≥ 1" and iub: "i < length xs" by auto
    then have xsin: "xs ! i ∈ A" using eq by auto
    define S where "S = (λ j. xs ! j) ` {0..<i}"
    then have "S = set (take i xs)"
      by (simp add: iub less_or_eq_imp_le nth_image)
    then have "xs ! i ∉ S" using dis set_take_distinct_elem_not iub by simp
    then have "S ⊆ A - {(xs ! i)}"
      using ‹S = set (take i xs)› eq set_take_subset by fastforce 
    moreover have "S ≠ {}" using S_def ilb by (simp) 
    moreover have "𝒫((xs ! i) | (⋂ j ∈ {0..<i} . xs ! j)) = 𝒫((xs ! i) | (⋂ Aj ∈ S . Aj))" 
      using S_def by auto
    ultimately show "𝒫((xs ! i) | (⋂ j ∈ {0..<i} . xs ! j)) ≥ f (xs ! i)"
      using assms(5) xsin by auto
  qed
  then have "(∏i = 1..<(length xs) . 𝒫((xs ! i) | (⋂ j ∈ {0..<i} . xs ! j))) ≥ 
    (∏i = 1..<(length xs) . f (xs ! i))"
    by (meson assms(4) prod_mono)
  moreover have "(∏i = 1..<(length xs) . f (xs ! i)) = (∏a ∈ A - {hd xs} . f a)"
  proof -
    have ne: "xs ≠ []" using assms(1) eq by auto
    have "A = (λ j. xs ! j) ` {0..<length xs}" using eq
      by (simp add: nth_image) 
    have "A - {hd xs} = set (tl xs) " using dis
      by (metis Diff_insert_absorb distinct.simps(2) eq list.exhaust_sel list.set(2) ne)
    also have "... = (λ j. xs ! j) ` {1..<length xs}" using nth_image_tl ne by auto
    finally have Ahdeq: "A - {hd xs} = (λ j. xs ! j) ` {1..<length xs}" by simp
    have io: "inj_on (nth xs) {1..<length xs}" using inj_on_nth dis
      by (metis atLeastLessThan_iff) 
    have "(∏i = 1..<(length xs) . f (xs ! i)) = (∏i ∈ {1..<(length xs)} . f (xs ! i))" by simp
    also have "... = (∏i ∈ (λ j. xs ! j) ` {1..<length xs} . f i)" 
      using io by (simp add: prod.reindex_cong) 
    finally show ?thesis using Ahdeq
      using ‹(∏i = 1..<length xs. f (xs ! i)) = prod f ((!) xs ` {1..<length xs})› by presburger 
  qed
  ultimately have "prob (⋂A) ≥ f (hd xs) * (∏a ∈ A - {hd xs} . f a)"
    using pA ‹f (hd xs) ≤ prob (hd xs)› assms(4) ordered_comm_semiring_class.comm_mult_left_mono
    by (simp add: mult_mono' prod_nonneg)  
  then show ?thesis
    by (metis ‹hd xs ∈ A› assms(3) prod.remove) 
qed

Theorem (Differential Privacy for Real Lists):
Given two non-empty lists of real numbers, `xs` and `ys`, with equal length `n`, and a privacy parameter `ε`, the probability of an individual element `i` being equal in both lists is bounded by the product of two exponential factors. Specifically, the probability that an element `j` in `xs` equals `i` is at most `(exp(ε))` times the probability that an element `j` in `ys` equals `i`, and vice versa.

lemma DP_RNM'_M_i:
  fixes xs ys :: "real list" and i n :: nat
  assumes lxs: "length xs = n"
    and lys: "length ys = n"
    and adj: "list_all2 (λ x y. x ≥ y ∧ x ≤ y + 1) xs ys"
  shows "𝒫(j in (RNM' xs). j = i) ≤ (exp ε) * 𝒫(j in (RNM' ys). j = i) ∧ 𝒫(j in (RNM' ys). j = i) ≤ (exp ε) * 𝒫(j in (RNM' xs). j = i)"
  using assms proof(cases"n = 0")
  case True
  hence xs: "xs = []" and ys: "ys = []"
    using lxs lys by blast+
  have 0: "RNM' [] = return (count_space UNIV) 0"using RNM'_Nil by auto
  thus ?thesis proof(cases"i = 0")
    case True
    hence 02: "𝒫(j in local.RNM' []. j = 0) = 1"unfolding 0 measure_def by auto
    show ?thesis unfolding xs ys True 02 using pose by auto
  next
    case False
    hence 02: "𝒫(j in local.RNM' []. j = i) = 0"unfolding 0 measure_def by auto
    show ?thesis unfolding xs ys 02 by auto
  qed
next
  case False
  have space_Lap_dist_multi [simp]: "⋀ xs b. space (Lap_dist_list b xs) = UNIV"
    by (auto simp: sets_Lap_dist_list sets_eq_imp_space_eq)
  have space_RNM'_UNIV[simp]: "⋀xs. space (local.RNM' xs) = UNIV"
    unfolding RNM'_def by (metis empty_not_UNIV sets_return space_Lap_dist_multi space_bind space_count_space)
  hence space_RNM'_UNIV2[simp]: "⋀xs i. {j. j∈ space (RNM' xs) ∧ j = i} = {i}"
    by auto

  thus ?thesis proof(cases"i < n")
    case True
    define x where x: "x = nth xs i"
    define y where y: "y = nth ys i"
    define xs2 where xs2: "xs2 = (list_exclude i xs)"
    define ys2 where ys2: "ys2 = (list_exclude i ys)"
    have xs: "xs = (list_insert x xs2 i)"
      by (metis length_0_conv length_greater_0_conv list_insert'_is_list_insert lxs cong_nth_total_nth False True insert_exclude x xs2)
    have ys: "ys = (list_insert y ys2 i)"
      by (metis length_0_conv length_greater_0_conv list_insert'_is_list_insert lys cong_nth_total_nth False True insert_exclude y ys2)
    obtain m :: nat where n: "n = Suc m"using True False not0_implies_Suc by blast
    have lxs2: "length xs2 = m"
      by (metis One_nat_def True add.assoc add.commute add_left_imp_eq id_take_nth_drop length_append list.size(4) list_exclude_def lxs n plus_1_eq_Suc xs2)
    have lys2: "length ys2 = m"
      by (metis One_nat_def True add.assoc add.commute add_left_imp_eq id_take_nth_drop length_append list.size(4) list_exclude_def lys n plus_1_eq_Suc ys2)
    have ilessm: "i ≤ m"
      using True n by auto
    have 1: "take i xs2 = take i xs"

    have 3: "drop i xs2 = drop (Suc i) xs"

    have 4: "drop i ys2 = drop (Suc i) ys"

    from adj have 5: "list_all2 (λ x y. x ≥ y ∧ x ≤ y + 1) (take i xs2)(take i ys2)" and 6: "list_all2 (λ x y. x ≥ y ∧ x ≤ y + 1) (drop i xs2)(drop i ys2)"
      unfolding 1 2 3 4 using list_all2_takeI list_all2_dropI by blast+
    have adj': "x ≥ y ∧ x ≤ y + 1"

    have adj2: "list_all2 (λ x y. x ≥ y ∧ x ≤ y + 1) xs2 ys2"

    note * = DP_RNM_M_i[of xs2 m ys2 _ y x, OF lxs2 lys2 _ adj' adj2 ilessm]

Theorem (Complement of Probability for Actuarial Mathematics):
Given a real number \(x\), the probability that a random variable \(X\) is less than or equal to \(x\) is complemented by \(1 - \frac{l_x}{l_0}\), where \(l_x\) and \(l_0\) are specific measures related to the actuarial context.

lemma PX_compl_l_normal: "𝒫(ξ in 𝔐. X ξ ≤ x) = 1 - $l_x / $l_0" for x::real

Theorem (Sum of Probabilities in a Probability Space):
Given a finite index set \(I\) and two events \(P\) and \(Q\) in a probability space \(M\), if \(P\) is defined for all \(n \in I\) and \(Q\) is an event, and there exists a unique \(n \in I\) such that \(P n\) implies \(Q\), then the probability of \(Q\) is equal to the sum of the probabilities of \(P n\) for all \(n \in I\). Mathematically, this is expressed as \(\Pr(Q) = \sum_{n \in I} \Pr(P n)\).

lemma (in prob_space) prob_sum:
  assumes [simp, intro]: "finite I"
  assumes P: "⋀n. n ∈ I ⟹ {x∈space M. P n x} ∈ events"
  assumes Q: "{x∈space M. Q x} ∈ events"
  assumes ae: "AE x in M. (∀n∈I. P n x ⟶ Q x) ∧ (Q x ⟶ (∃!n∈I. P n x))"
  shows "𝒫(x in M. Q x) = (∑n∈I. 𝒫(x in M. P n x))"
proof -
  from ae[THEN AE_E_prob] obtain S
    where S:
      "S ⊆ {x ∈ space M. (∀n∈I. P n x ⟶ Q x) ∧ (Q x ⟶ (∃!n. n ∈ I ∧ P n x))}"
      "S ∈ events"
      "prob S = 1"
    by auto
  then have disj: "disjoint_family_on (λn. {x∈space M. P n x} ∩ S) I"
    by (auto simp: disjoint_family_on_def)
  from S have ae_S:
    "AE x in M. x ∈ {x∈space M. Q x} ⟷ x ∈ (⋃n∈I. {x∈space M. P n x} ∩ S)"
    "⋀n. n ∈ I ⟹ AE x in M. x ∈ {x∈space M. P n x} ⟷ x ∈ {x∈space M. P n x} ∩ S"
    using ae by (auto dest!: AE_prob_1)
  from ae_S have *:
    "𝒫(x in M. Q x) = prob (⋃n∈I. {x∈space M. P n x} ∩ S)"
    using P Q S by (intro finite_measure_eq_AE) (auto intro!: sets.Int)
  from ae_S have **:
    "⋀n. n ∈ I ⟹ 𝒫(x in M. P n x) = prob ({x∈space M. P n x} ∩ S)"
    using P Q S by (intro finite_measure_eq_AE) auto
  show ?thesis
    using S P disj
    by (auto simp add: * ** simp del: UN_simps intro!: finite_measure_finite_Union)
qed

Theorem (Probability of Sample Geometric Distribution):
Given a geometric distribution with parameter \(n\), the probability that a randomly selected sample is less than or equal to \(2^j\) is bounded by \(1/2^j\), formally expressed as \(\text{measure}(\text{sample\_pro}(\text{geom\_pro}(n))) \leq 1/2^j\).

This theorem relates to the study of universal hash families, where geometric distributions are used to analyze the performance and security of cryptographic hash functions and randomized algorithms in data structures. It quantifies the likelihood of outcomes within a geometric probability space, ensuring that the distribution of sample points adheres to a specific probabilistic constraint.

lemma geom_pro_prob_single:
  "measure (sample_pro (geom_pro n)) {j} ≤ 1 / 2^j" (is "?L ≤ ?R")
proof -
  have "?L = measure (sample_pro (geom_pro n)) ({j..}-{j+1..})"
    by (intro measure_pmf_cong) auto
  also have "... = measure (sample_pro (geom_pro n)) {j..} - measure (sample_pro (geom_pro n)) {j+1..}"
    by (intro measure_Diff) auto
  also have "... = measure (sample_pro (geom_pro n)) {ω. ω ≥ j}-measure (sample_pro (geom_pro n)) {ω. ω ≥ (j+1)}"
    by (intro arg_cong2[where f="(-)"] measure_pmf_cong) auto
  also have "... = of_bool (j ≤ n) * 1 / 2 ^ j - of_bool (j + 1 ≤ n) / 2 ^ (j + 1)"
    unfolding geom_pro_prob by simp
  also have "... ≤ 1/2^j - 0"
    by (intro diff_mono) auto
  also have "... = ?R" by simp
  finally show ?thesis by simp
qed

Theorem (Distribution of Elements in Cardinality Estimation):
Given a randomized data structure for estimating the cardinality of a set, the probability that a randomly chosen element's value is less than or equal to two-thirds of another element's value is bounded above by three-fifths of the latter element's value. Mathematically, this is expressed as \(\rho(\frac{2}{3} \cdot b) \leq \frac{3}{5} \cdot b\).

lemma rho_two_thirds: "ρ (2/3 * b) ≤ 3/5 *b"
proof -
  have "1/3 ≤ exp ( - 13 / 12::real )"
    by (approximation 8)
  also have "... ≤ exp ( - 1 - 2 / real b )"
    using b_min by (intro iffD2[OF exp_le_cancel_iff]) (simp add:algebra_simps)
  also have "... ≤ exp ( b * (-(1/real b)-2*(1/real b)^2))"
    using b_min by (simp add:algebra_simps power2_eq_square)
  also have  "... ≤ exp ( b * ln (1-1/real b))"
    using b_min
    by (intro iffD2[OF exp_le_cancel_iff] mult_left_mono ln_one_minus_pos_lower_bound) auto
  also have "... = exp ( ln ( (1-1/real b) powr b))"
    using b_min by (subst ln_powr) auto
  also have "... = (1-1/real b) powr b"
    using b_min by (subst exp_ln) auto
  finally have a:"1/3 ≤ (1-1/real b) powr b" by simp

  have "2/5 ≤ (1/3) powr (2/3::real)"
    by (approximation 5)
  also have "... ≤ ((1-1/real b) powr b) powr (2/3)"
    by (intro powr_mono2 a) auto
  also have "... = (1-1/real b) powr (2/3 * real b)"
    by (subst powr_powr) (simp add:algebra_simps)
  finally have "2/5 ≤ (1 - 1 / real b) powr (2 / 3 * real b)" by simp
  hence "1 - (1 - 1 / real b) powr (2 / 3 * real b) ≤ 3/5"
    by simp
  hence "ρ (2/3 * b) ≤ b * (3/5)"
    unfolding ρ_def by (intro mult_left_mono) auto
  thus ?thesis
    by simp
qed

Theorem (Law of Cosines for Complex Geometry):

Mathematically, it is expressed as:
\[(\text{cdist}_C \text{ B})^2 = (\text{cdist}_A \text{ C})^2 + (\text{cdist}_A \text{ B})^2 - 2 \cdot (\text{cdist}_A \text{ C}) \cdot (\text{cdist}_A \text{ B}) \cdot \cos(\angle(\text{C}-\text{A})(\text{B}-\text{A}))\]

lemma law_of_cosines:
  shows "(cdist B C)⇧2 = (cdist A C)⇧2 + (cdist A B)⇧2 - 2*(cdist A C)*(cdist A B)*(cos (∠ (C-A) (B-A)))"

  let ?a = "C-B" and ?b = "C-A" and ?c = "B-A"
  have "?a = ?b - ?c"

  hence "(cmod ?a)⇧2 = (cmod (?b - ?c))⇧2"
    by metis
  also have "... = Re (scalprod (?b-?c) (?b-?c))"
    by (simp add: cmod_square)
  also have "... = (cmod ?b)⇧2 + (cmod ?c)⇧2 - 2*Re (scalprod ?b ?c)"
    by (simp add: cmod_square field_simps)
  finally

    using cos_cmod_scalprod[of ?b ?c]
    by simp
qed

Theorem (Cosine Rule for Triangle Side Lengths):
Given three points a, b, and c in the Euclidean plane, the square of the length of the side opposite to point a (denoted as side a) is equal to the sum of the squares of the lengths of the other two sides minus twice the product of the lengths of the other two sides and their respective projection onto the line containing side a. Mathematically, this is expressed as:

\((norm\_dist(a, c))^2 = (norm\_dist(a, b))^2 + (norm\_dist(b, c))^2 - 2 \cdot (a - b) \cdot (b - c)\)

This theorem is a consequence of Tarski's axioms for Euclidean geometry and is valid except in the context of the Euclidean plane, where it does not hold (hence the reference to Tarski's axioms).

lemma cosine_rule:
  fixes a b c :: "real ^ ('n::finite)"
  shows "(norm_dist a c)⇧2 =
  (norm_dist a b)⇧2 + (norm_dist b c)⇧2 + 2 * ((a - b) ∙ (b - c))"
proof -
  have "(a - b) + (b - c) = a - c" by simp
  with dot_norm [of "a - b" "b - c"]
    have "(a - b) ∙ (b - c) =
        ((norm (a - c))⇧2 - (norm (a - b))⇧2 - (norm (b - c))⇧2) / 2"
      by simp
  thus ?thesis by simp
qed

Theorem (Cosine Law for Triangles):
Given a triangle with vertices A, B, and C, the square of the length of side BC (opposite angle A) is equal to the sum of the squares of the lengths of sides AB and AC, minus twice the product of the lengths of sides AB and AC and the cosine of angle BAC. Mathematically, it is expressed as \(2 \cdot \text{dist}(A, B) \cdot \text{dist}(A, C) \cdot \cos(\angle BAC) = \text{dist}(A, B)^2 + \text{dist}(A, C)^2 - \text{dist}(B, C)^2\).

lemma cosine_law_triangle':
  "2 * dist a b * dist a c * cos (angle b a c) = (dist a b ^ 2 + dist a c ^ 2 - dist b c ^ 2)"
  using cosine_law_triangle[of b c a] by simp

Theorem (Cosine Law for Triangles):
Given a triangle with vertices A, B, and C, the cosine of angle BAC is given by the formula:
\[
\cos(BAC) = \frac{AB^2 + AC^2 - BC^2}{2 \cdot AB \cdot AC}
\]
This theorem relates the lengths of the sides of a triangle to the cosine of one of its angles.

lemma cosine_law_triangle'':
  "cos (angle b a c) = (dist a b ^ 2 + dist a c ^ 2 - dist b c ^ 2) / (2 * dist a b * dist a c)"
  using cosine_law_triangle[of b c a] by simp

Theorem (Cosine Law for Triangles):
Given a triangle with vertices A, B, and C, the square of the length of side BC (denoted as \(b^2\)) is equal to the sum of the squares of the lengths of sides AB (denoted as \(a^2\)) and AC (denoted as \(c^2\)), minus twice the product of the lengths of sides AB and AC and the cosine of the angle at vertex A (angle BAC). Mathematically, it is expressed as \(b^2 = a^2 + c^2 - 2ac \cdot \cos(\angle BAC)\).

lemma cosine_law_triangle:
  "dist b c ^ 2 = dist a b ^ 2 + dist a c ^ 2 - 2 * dist a b * dist a c * cos (angle b a c)"
  using cosine_law_vector[of "b - a" "c - a"]
  by (simp add: dist_norm angle_def vangle_commute norm_minus_commute)

Theorem (Basic Geometric Properties of Triangles):
Given three points forming triangles, several angle relationships hold true. Specifically, corresponding angles formed by the intersection of lines through these points are equal. For instance, the angle formed by points b1, a1, c1 is equal to the angle formed by points b2, a2, c2, and so on. These relationships are fundamental in proving theorems related to isosceles triangles, sine and cosine rules, and triangle congruence.

lemma angles:
  "angle b1 a1 c1 = angle b2 a2 c2" "angle a1 b1 c1 = angle a2 b2 c2" "angle a1 c1 b1 = angle a2 c2 b2"
  "angle c1 a1 b1 = angle b2 a2 c2" "angle c1 b1 a1 = angle a2 b2 c2" "angle b1 c1 a1 = angle a2 c2 b2"
  "angle b1 a1 c1 = angle c2 a2 b2" "angle a1 b1 c1 = angle c2 b2 a2" "angle a1 c1 b1 = angle b2 c2 a2"
  "angle c1 a1 b1 = angle c2 a2 b2" "angle c1 b1 a1 = angle c2 b2 a2" "angle b1 c1 a1 = angle b2 c2 a2"
  using angles' by (simp_all add: angle_commute)

Theorem (Sine Law for Triangles):
Given a triangle with sides \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\), and angles opposite these sides as \(\angle C\), \(\angle B\), and \(\angle A\) respectively, if side \(b\) is not equal to side \(c\), then the sine of angle \(C\) is equal to the sine of angle \(B\) times the distance from point \(A\) to side \(C\) divided by the distance from point \(B\) to side \(C\), expressed as \(\sin(\angle C) = \frac{\sin(\angle B) \cdot \text{dist}(A, C)}{\text{dist}(B, C)}\).

lemma sine_law_triangle'':
  "b ≠ c ⟹ sin (angle c b a) = sin (angle b a c) * dist a c / dist b c"
  using sine_law_triangle[of a b c] by (simp add: divide_simps angle_commute)

Theorem (Sine Law for Triangles):
Given a triangle with sides \(b\), \(c\), and angle \(a\) opposite side \(b\), if side \(b\) is not equal to side \(c\), then the sine of angle \(a\) is proportional to the sine of angle \(b\) opposite side \(c\), with the ratio being the length of side \(a\) divided by the length of side \(c\). Mathematically, this is expressed as \(\sin(\angle a) = \frac{\sin(\angle b) \cdot \text{dist}(a, c)}{\text{dist}(b, c)}\).

lemma sine_law_triangle':
  "b ≠ c ⟹ sin (angle a b c) = sin (angle b a c) * dist a c / dist b c"
  using sine_law_triangle[of a b c] by (simp add: divide_simps)

Theorem (Law of Sines for Triangles):
Given a triangle with sides \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\), and angles \(\angle_c\), \(\angle_a\), and \(\angle_b\) opposite to these sides respectively, if no two sides are equal (\(a \neq b\), \(b \neq c\), \(a \neq c\)), then the following relationship holds: \(\sin(\angle_c) \cdot cdist(b, c) = \sin(\angle_c) \cdot cdist(c, a)\).

theorem law_of_sines:
  assumes h1:‹b ≠ a› ‹a ≠ c› ‹b ≠ c›
  shows  "sin (angle_c a b c) * cdist b c = sin (angle_c c a b) * cdist a c" (is "?A = ?B") 
proof - 
  {fix a b c ::complex
    have f0:‹sin (Arg (cnj c - cnj a)) = - sin (Arg ( c - a))›
      by (metis arg_cnj_not_pi arg_cnj_pi complex_cnj_diff neg_0_equal_iff_equal sin_minus
          sin_pi)
    have f1:‹cos (Arg (cnj c - cnj a)) = cos (Arg (c - a))›
      by (metis arg_cnj_not_pi arg_cnj_pi complex_cnj_diff cos_minus)
    assume ‹b-a ≠ 0› ‹c-a ≠ 0 ›
    then have f2: ‹b-a = cmod (b-a) * cis (Arg (b-a)) ∧ cnj (c-a) = cmod (c-a) * cis (Arg (cnj (c-a)))›
      using rcis_cmod_Arg rcis_def 
      by (metis complex_mod_cnj)
    then have ‹Im(cis (Arg (b-a)) * cis (Arg (cnj(c-a)))) = sin (angle_c c a b)›
      unfolding ang_vec_def angle_c_def using f1 f0 by(auto simp:cis.code sin_diff) 
    then have ‹Im (cmod (b-a) * cis (Arg (b-a)) * cmod (c-a) * cis (Arg (cnj (c-a)))) =
      cmod (c-a) *cmod (b-a) * sin (angle_c c a b) ›
      by (metis Im_complex_of_real[of "cmod (c - a)"] Im_complex_of_real[of "cmod (b - a)"]
          Im_mult_real[of "cor (cmod (c - a))"
            "cis (Arg (cnj (c - a))) * (cor (cmod (b - a)) * cis (Arg (b - a)))"]
          Im_mult_real[of "cor (cmod (b - a))" "cis (Arg (b - a)) * cis (Arg (cnj (c - a)))"]
          Re_complex_of_real[of "cmod (c - a)"] Re_complex_of_real[of "cmod (b - a)"]
          ab_semigroup_mult_class.mult_ac(1)[of "cor (cmod (b - a))" "cis (Arg (b - a))"
            "cis (Arg (cnj (c - a)))"]
          ab_semigroup_mult_class.mult_ac(1)[of "cis (Arg (cnj (c - a)))"
            "cor (cmod (b - a)) * cis (Arg (b - a))" "cor (cmod (c - a))"]
          ab_semigroup_mult_class.mult_ac(1)[of "cmod (c - a)" "cmod (b - a)"
            "Im (cis (Arg (b - a)) * cis (Arg (cnj (c - a))))"]
          mult.commute[of "cis (Arg (cnj (c - a)))" "cor (cmod (b - a)) * cis (Arg (b - a))"]
          mult.commute[of "cis (Arg (cnj (c - a))) * (cor (cmod (b - a)) * cis (Arg (b - a)))"
            "cor (cmod (c - a))"]
          mult.commute[of "cor (cmod (b - a)) * cis (Arg (b - a)) * cor (cmod (c - a))"
            "cis (Arg (cnj (c - a)))"])
    then have ‹Im ((b-a)*cnj(c-a)) = cmod (c-a) *cmod (b-a) * sin (angle_c c a b)› 
      using ang_sin by presburger
  }note ang=this
  have i2:‹sin (angle_c c a b) = Im((b-a)*cnj(c-a))/ (cmod(b-a)*cmod(c-a))›
    using ang[of b a c] h1 by(auto)
  have ‹sin (angle_c a b c) = Im((c-b)*cnj(a-b)) / (cmod (c-b)*cmod (a-b))›
    using ang h1 by(auto)
  then have imp1:‹cmod (c-b) * sin (angle_c a b c) = Im((c-b)*cnj(a-b)) / (cmod (a-b)) ›
    by auto
  from i2 have imp2:‹cmod (c-a) * sin (angle_c c a b) = Im((b-a)*cnj(c-a))/ (cmod(b-a)) ›
    by auto
  show ?thesis using imp1 imp2 by(auto simp:field_simps norm_minus_commute) 
qed

Theorem (Sine Law for Triangles):
In any triangle, the product of the sine of an angle and the opposite side length is constant. Specifically, for angles A, B, and C, the relationship \(\sin(A) \cdot \text{dist}_{BC} = \sin(B) \cdot \text{dist}_{AC}\) holds true.

lemma sine_law_triangle:
  "sin (angle a b c) * dist b c = sin (angle b a c) * dist a c" (is "?A = ?B")
proof (cases "a = b")
  assume neq: "a ≠ b"
  show ?thesis
  proof (rule power2_eq_imp_eq)
    from neq have "(sin (angle a b c) * dist b c) ^ 2 * dist a b ^ 2 =
                     dist a b ^ 2 * dist b c ^ 2 - ((a - b) ∙ (c - b)) ^ 2"
      by (simp add: sin_squared_eq cos_angle dist_commute field_simps)
    also have "… = dist a b ^ 2 * dist a c ^ 2 - ((b - a) ∙ (c - a)) ^ 2"
      by (simp only: dist_norm power2_norm_eq_inner)
         (simp add: power2_eq_square algebra_simps inner_commute)
    also from neq have "… = (sin (angle b a c) * dist a c) ^ 2 * dist a b ^ 2"
      by (simp add: sin_squared_eq cos_angle dist_commute field_simps)
    finally show "?A^2 = ?B^2" using neq by (subst (asm) mult_cancel_right) simp_all
  qed (auto intro!: mult_nonneg_nonneg sin_angle_nonneg)
qed simp_all

Given a triangle with sides \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\), and angles \(\angle_c\) at vertex \(C\), the Law of Sines states that the product of the sine of \(\angle_c\) and the side opposite it (\(c\)) is equal to the product of the sine of the angle at vertex \(B\) and its opposite side (\(a\)). Mathematically, it is expressed as \(\sin(\angle_c) \cdot cdist(b, a) = \sin(\angle_b) \cdot cdist(a, c)\).

Theorem (Cosine of Angles Equality Implies Angle Equality):
If the cosine of two angles, \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) are equal to the cosine of two other angles, \(d\), \(e\), and \(f\) respectively, then the angles themselves are equal, i.e., \(\cos(\angle a, b, c) = \cos(\angle d, e, f) \Rightarrow \angle a, b, c = \angle d, e, f\).

lemma cos_angle_eqD: "cos (angle a b c) = cos (angle d e f) ⟹ angle a b c = angle d e f"
  unfolding angle_def by (rule cos_vangle_eqD)

Theorem (The Geometric Relationship of Cyclic Quadrilaterals):
For any cyclic quadrilateral, the sum of a pair of opposite sides is equal to the total length of the other two pairs when measured in the same unit. This theorem provides an important relationship between the side lengths and diagonals within such geometric figures.

Theorem (Ptolemy's Theorem for Cyclic Quadrilaterals):
Given a quadrilateral ABCD inscribed in a circle with center O, where the distances from O to vertices A, B, C, and D are equal to the circle's radius, Ptolemy's theorem states that the product of the diagonals AC and BD equals the sum of the products of opposite sides AB and CD, and AD and BC. Mathematically, this is expressed as \( \text{dist}(A, C) \cdot \text{dist}(B, D) = \text{dist}(A, B) \cdot \text{dist}(C, D) + \text{dist}(A, D) \cdot \text{dist}(B, C) \).

theorem ptolemy:
  fixes A B C D center :: "real ^ 2"
  assumes "dist center A = radius" and "dist center B = radius"
  assumes "dist center C = radius" and "dist center D = radius"
  assumes ordering_of_points:
    "radiant_of (A - center) ≤ radiant_of (B - center)"
    "radiant_of (B - center) ≤ radiant_of (C - center)"
    "radiant_of (C - center) ≤ radiant_of (D - center)"
  shows "dist A C * dist B D = dist A B * dist C D + dist A D * dist B C"
proof -
  from ‹dist center A = radius› have "0 ≤ radius" by auto
  define α β γ δ
    where "α = radiant_of (A - center)" and "β = radiant_of (B - center)"
    and "γ = radiant_of (C - center)" and "δ = radiant_of (D - center)"
  from ordering_of_points have angle_basics:
    "α ≤ β" "β ≤ γ" "γ ≤ δ"
    "0 ≤ α" "α ≤ 2 * pi" "0 ≤ β" "β ≤ 2 * pi"
    "0 ≤ γ" "γ ≤ 2 * pi" "0 ≤ δ" "δ ≤ 2 * pi"
    unfolding α_def β_def γ_def δ_def by auto
  from assms(1-4) have
    "A = center + radius *⇩R of_radiant α" "B = center + radius *⇩R of_radiant β"
    "C = center + radius *⇩R of_radiant γ" "D = center + radius *⇩R of_radiant δ"
    unfolding α_def β_def γ_def δ_def
    using relative_polar_form_eq dist_commute by metis+

  from this have dist_eqs:
    "dist A C = 2 * radius * sin ((γ - α) / 2)"
    "dist B D = 2 * radius * sin ((δ - β) / 2)"
    "dist A B = 2 * radius * sin ((β - α) / 2)"
    "dist C D = 2 * radius * sin ((δ - γ) / 2)"
    "dist A D = 2 * radius * sin ((δ - α) / 2)"
    "dist B C = 2 * radius * sin ((γ - β) / 2)"
    using angle_basics ‹radius ≥ 0› dist_circle_segment by (auto)

  have "dist A C * dist B D = 4 * radius ^ 2 * sin ((γ - α) / 2) * sin ((δ - β) / 2)"
    unfolding dist_eqs by (simp add: power2_eq_square)
  also have "… = 4 * radius ^ 2 * (sin ((β - α) / 2) * sin ((δ - γ) / 2) + sin ((γ - β) / 2) * sin ((δ - α) / 2))"
  proof -
    define ω⇩1 ω⇩2 ω⇩3 where "ω⇩1 = (β - α) / 2" and "ω⇩2 = (γ - β) / 2" and "ω⇩3 = (δ - γ) / 2"
    have "(γ - α) / 2 = ω⇩1 + ω⇩2" and "(δ - β) / 2 = ω⇩2 + ω⇩3" and "(δ - α) / 2 = ω⇩1 + ω⇩2 + ω⇩3"
      unfolding ω⇩1_def ω⇩2_def ω⇩3_def by (auto simp add: field_simps)
    have "sin ((γ - α) / 2) * sin ((δ - β) / 2) = sin (ω⇩1 + ω⇩2) * sin (ω⇩2 + ω⇩3)"
      using ‹(γ - α) / 2 = ω⇩1 + ω⇩2› ‹(δ - β) / 2 = ω⇩2 + ω⇩3› by (simp only:)
    also have "… = sin ω⇩1 * sin ω⇩3 + sin ω⇩2 * sin (ω⇩1 + ω⇩2 + ω⇩3)"
      by (rule ptolemy_trigonometric)
    also have "… = (sin ((β - α) / 2) * sin ((δ - γ) / 2) + sin ((γ - β) / 2) * sin ((δ - α) / 2))"
      using ω⇩1_def ω⇩2_def ω⇩3_def ‹(δ - α) / 2 = ω⇩1 + ω⇩2 + ω⇩3› by (simp only:)
    finally show ?thesis by simp
  qed
  also have "… = dist A B * dist C D + dist A D * dist B C"
    unfolding dist_eqs by (simp add: distrib_left power2_eq_square)
  finally show ?thesis .
qed

Theorem (Ptolemy's Theorem for Circles):
Given a cyclic quadrilateral inscribed in a circle, the product of the lengths of the diagonals equals the sum of the products of the lengths of opposite sides. Formally, if \(AC \cdot BD = AB \cdot CD + BC \cdot AD\), where \(AB\), \(BC\), \(CD\), and \(AD\) are the sides of the quadrilateral and \(AC\), \(BD\) are the diagonals.

Theorem (Ptolemy's Theorem):
Using polar coordinates and trigonometric identities, we can analytically prove Ptolemy's theorem. This theorem relates the sides and diagonals of a cyclic quadrilateral, showing that the product of the lengths of the diagonals equals the sum of the products of the lengths of opposite sides.

lemma nth_of_radiant_2 [simp]:

unfolding of_radiant_def by simp

Theorem (Ptolemy's Theorem in Polar Form):
Given a cyclic quadrilateral, the relationship between the sides and diagonals can be expressed using polar coordinates. Specifically, the difference in the angles (ω) of the diagonals, when reduced by 2π, is equivalent to the original angle (ω), demonstrating the cyclic nature of the quadrilateral.

lemma of_radiant_minus_2pi:
  "of_radiant (ω - 2 * pi) = of_radiant ω"
proof -
  have "of_radiant (ω - 2 * pi) = of_radiant (ω - 2 * pi + 2 * pi)"
    by (simp only: of_radiant_plus_2pi)
  also have "… = of_radiant ω" by simp
  finally show ?thesis .
qed

Theorem (Ptolemy's Theorem in Radiant Measure):
Given a cyclic quadrilateral, the sum of the products of the opposite sides is equal to the product of the diagonals, when measured in radiant degrees. This is expressed as \(0 \leq \text{radiant\_of}(p) < 2\pi\), where \(p\) represents the cyclic quadrilateral's sides and diagonals.

lemma radiant_of_bounds [simp]:
  "0 ≤ radiant_of p" "radiant_of p < 2 * pi"
using radiant_of by auto

Theorem (Ptolemy's Theorem in Polar Coordinates):
Given a cyclic quadrilateral, the sum of the products of the lengths of the opposite sides equals the product of the lengths of the diagonals. In polar coordinates, this translates to the equality of the sine of the sum of angles to the sum of sines of the angles, formalized using trigonometric identities.

Given a function \(f\), the product of \(f\) evaluated at consecutive natural numbers from 1 to 2 is equal to the product of \(f\) evaluated at 1 and 2, that is, \(f(1) \cdot f(2) = \prod_{n=1}^{2} f(n)\).

Theorem (Cross Product Compatibility with Diagonal Functor):
Given a function \( f: X \rightarrow Y \) between two sets, the cross product of \( f \) with itself, when composed with the diagonal functor applied to \( X \), yields the same result as applying \( f \) to the diagonal functor applied to \( Y \).

lemma cfunc_cross_prod_comp_diagonal:
  assumes "f: X → Y" 
  shows "(f ×⇩f f) ∘⇩c diagonal(X) = diagonal(Y) ∘⇩c f"

proof -
  have "(f ×⇩f f) ∘⇩c ⟨id⇩c X, id⇩c X⟩ = ⟨f ∘⇩c id⇩c X, f ∘⇩c id⇩c X⟩"

This lemma states that the product of a list of functions applied to a range of natural numbers is equivalent to the product of the function applied to the set of those numbers. Theorem (Cartesian Product of a Set and a Latin Square):
Given a set \(A\) and a Latin square \(B\), for any element \(a\) in \(A\), the set of ordered pairs \((a, b)\) where \(b\) is from \(B\) and the first component is \(a\) is equivalent to the Cartesian product of \(A\) with \(B\), that is, \(\{ (a, b) \in A \times B \mid fst (a, b) = a \} = A \times B\).

This theorem relates to the structure of Latin squares, where each number appears exactly once in each row and column, and extends the concept to the Cartesian product of a set with a Latin square.

shows "{p∈A×B. fst p = a} = {a}×B"
using SigmaI assms by auto

Theorem (Appending Sets in Univariate Real Arithmetic):
Given two lists of natural numbers, if each list's elements are less than the length of another list, the sum of the first list appended to the sum of the second list, when both are appended to a third list, equals the product of the first list and the second list appended to the third list.
Mathematically: \(z_R((fst xs) + (length as), (snd xs) + (length as))(as + bs) = xs * ys \cdot as \cdot bs\)

lemma z_append_R:
  fixes xs:: "(nat list * nat list)"
  assumes "⋀i. i ∈ set (fst xs) ⟹ i  < length as"
  assumes "⋀i. i ∈ set (snd xs) ⟹ i  < length as"
  shows "z_R ((fst xs) @ (map ((+) (length as)) (fst ys)), (snd xs) @ (map ((+) (length as)) (snd ys))) (as @ bs) = z_R xs as * z_R ys bs"
proof -
  have 1: "map ((!) (as @ bs)) (fst xs) = map ((!) as) (fst xs)"
    unfolding list_eq_iff_nth_eq
    using assms by (auto simp add:nth_append)
  have 2: "map ((!) (as @ bs) ∘ (+) (length as)) (fst ys) = map ((!) bs) (fst ys)"
    unfolding list_eq_iff_nth_eq
    using assms by auto
  have 3: "map ((!) (as @ bs)) (snd xs) = map ((!) as) (snd xs)"
    unfolding list_eq_iff_nth_eq
    using assms by (auto simp add:nth_append)
  have 4: "map ((!) (as @ bs) ∘ (+) (length as)) (snd ys) = map ((!) bs) (snd ys)"
    unfolding list_eq_iff_nth_eq
    using assms by auto
  show ?thesis
    unfolding z_R_def apply auto
    unfolding 1 2 3 4 apply (auto)
    by (smt (z3) assms(1) comp_apply length_map map_append map_eq_conv map_sgas_def nth_append nth_append_length_plus) 
qed

Theorem (Equality of Mappings on Lists):
Given two functions \(f\) and \(g\), and two lists \(X\) and \(Y\) of equal length, \(f\) maps \(X\) to \(Y\) if and only if \(g\) maps \(Y\) to \(X\) and each corresponding element in \(X\) and \(Y\) is equal under the functions \(f\) and \(g\). Theorem (Parametric Solution for Inequality of Sums):
Given two non-zero vectors x and y, where the absolute value of y is less than or equal to the absolute value of x, and indices j, k, l are positive integers with specific constraints, we can express the product of x and y (x⇧@j * y⇧@k) as z⇧@l under certain conditions. There are five cases (A to E) that describe how x, y, and z can be related through a common scalar r, q, and t, considering their indices and properties like length, rotation, and primitivity.

theorem LS_parametric_solution:
  assumes y_le_x: "❙|y❙| ≤ ❙|x❙|"
    and j_min: "1 ≤ j"  and k_min: "1 ≤ k" and l_min: "2 ≤ l"
  shows
    "x⇧@j ⋅ y⇧@k = z⇧@l
  ⟷
    (∃r m n t.
        x = r⇧@m ∧ y = r⇧@n ∧ z = r⇧@t ∧ m*j+n*k=t*l) ―‹Case A: {x,y} is not a code›
  ∨ (j = 1 ∧ k = 1) ∧
    (∃r q m n.
        x = (r⋅q)⇧@m⋅r ∧ y = q⋅(r⋅q)⇧@n ∧ z = r⋅q ∧ m + n + 1 = l ∧ r⋅q ≠ q⋅r) ― ‹Case B›
  ∨ (j = 1 ∧ 2 ≤ k) ∧
    (∃r q.
        x = (q⋅r⇧@k)⇧@(l-1)⋅q ∧ y = r ∧ z = q⋅r⇧@k ∧ r⋅q ≠ q⋅r) ― ‹Case C›
  ∨ (j = 1 ∧ 2 ≤ k) ∧
    (∃r q t. 0 < t ∧
        x = ((q ⋅ r) ⋅ (r ⋅ (q ⋅ r) ⇧@ t) ⇧@ (k - 1)) ⇧@ (l - 2)⋅(((q ⋅ r) ⋅
               (r ⋅ (q ⋅ r) ⇧@ t) ⇧@ (k - 2)) ⋅ r) ⋅ q
        ∧ y = r ⋅ (q ⋅ r) ⇧@ t
        ∧ z = (q ⋅ r) ⋅ (r ⋅ (q ⋅ r) ⇧@ t) ⇧@ (k - 1)
        ∧ r⋅q ≠ q⋅r) ― ‹Case D›
  ∨ (j = 2 ∧ k = 1 ∧ l = 2) ∧
    (∃r q t. 2 ≤ t ∧
        x = (r ⋅ q) ⇧@ t ⋅ r ∧ y = q ⋅ r ⋅ r ⋅ q
        ∧ z = (r ⋅ q) ⇧@ t ⋅ r ⋅ r ⋅ q  ∧ r⋅q ≠ q⋅r ) ― ‹Case E›
  "
    (is "?eq =
   (?sol_per ∨ (?cond_j1k1 ∧ ?sol_j1k1) ∨
   (?cond_j1k2 ∧ ?sol_j1k2_b) ∨
   (?cond_j1k2 ∧ ?sol_j1k2_a) ∨
   (?cond_j2k1l2 ∧ ?sol_j2k1l2))")
proof(rule iffI)
  assume eq: "x ⇧@ j ⋅ y ⇧@ k = z ⇧@ l"
  show
    "(?sol_per ∨ (?cond_j1k1 ∧ ?sol_j1k1) ∨
   (?cond_j1k2 ∧ ?sol_j1k2_b) ∨
   (?cond_j1k2 ∧ ?sol_j1k2_a) ∨
   (?cond_j2k1l2 ∧ ?sol_j2k1l2))"
  proof(cases)
    assume "x⋅y = y⋅x"
    from comm_primrootE'[OF this]
    obtain r m n where "x = r ⇧@ m" "y = r ⇧@ n" "primitive r".

    note eqs = eq[unfolded this, folded pow_mult, folded pow_add[of "m*j" "n*k" r ], symmetric]
    obtain t where "z = r ⇧@ t"

    from eqs[unfolded this, folded pow_mult, symmetric]
    have "m * j + n * k = t * l"
      unfolding prim_nemp[OF ‹primitive r›, THEN eq_pow_exp].
    hence ?sol_per
      using ‹x = r ⇧@ m› ‹y = r ⇧@ n› ‹z = r ⇧@ t› by blast
    thus ?thesis
      by blast
  next
    assume "x⋅y ≠ y⋅x"
    interpret LS_len_le x y j k l z
      using ‹x ⇧@ j ⋅ y ⇧@ k = z ⇧@ l› ‹x⋅y ≠ y⋅x› j_min k_min l_min y_le_x
      by(unfold_locales)

    show ?thesis
      using solution_cases
    proof(cases)
      case 1
      from case_j2k1[OF less_or_eq_imp_le[of 2 j] ‹k = 1›, OF disjI2, OF ‹j = 2›[symmetric], of "?sol_j2k1l2 ∧ l = 2"]
      have "?sol_j2k1l2" and "l = 2"
        by auto
      thus ?thesis
        using ‹k = 1› ‹j = 2› by blast
    next
      case 2
      have "?sol_j1k2_a"
        using case_j1k2_a[OF ‹j = 1› ‹2 ≤ k› ssufD1[OF ‹z <s y ⇧@ k›], of ?sol_j1k2_a]
        unfolding Suc_eq_plus1
        by blast
      thus ?thesis
        using ‹j = 1› ‹2 ≤ k› by blast
    next
      case 3
      with case_j1k2_b[OF this, of "?sol_j1k2_b"]

      thus ?thesis
        using ‹j = 1› ‹2 ≤ k› by blast
    next

        unfolding Suc_eq_plus1 shift_pow
        by blast

        using ‹j = 1› ‹k = 1› by blast
    qed
  qed
next
  have "l ≠ 0" "l - 1 ≠ 0"
    using l_min by auto
  have "k ≠ 0" using k_min by auto
  have "j ≠ 0" using j_min by auto
  assume   "(?sol_per ∨ (?cond_j1k1 ∧ ?sol_j1k1) ∨
   (?cond_j1k2 ∧ ?sol_j1k2_b) ∨
   (?cond_j1k2 ∧ ?sol_j1k2_a) ∨
   (?cond_j2k1l2 ∧ ?sol_j2k1l2))"
  then show ?eq
  proof(elim disjE conjE exE)
    fix r m n t
    assume sol: "x = r ⇧@ m" "y = r ⇧@ n" "z = r ⇧@ t"
      and "m * j + n * k = t * l"
    show ?thesis
      unfolding sol
      unfolding pow_mult[symmetric] pow_add[symmetric]
      unfolding ‹m * j + n * k = t * l›..
  next
    fix r q m n
    assume "j = 1" "k = 1" and sol: "x = (r⋅q)⇧@m⋅r"
      "y = q⋅(r⋅q)⇧@n" "z = r⋅q"
      and "m + n + 1 = l"

    show ?thesis
      unfolding sol
      unfolding ‹j = 1› ‹k = 1› ‹Suc (m + n) = l›[symmetric] pow_list_1
      unfolding lassoc pow_Suc pow_add
      unfolding pow_comm[of m, symmetric] lassoc..
  next
    fix r q
    assume "j = 1" "2 ≤ k" and sol: "x = (q ⋅ r ⇧@ k) ⇧@ (l - 1) ⋅ q" "y = r" "z = q ⋅ r ⇧@ k"
    have "0 < l"
      using ‹2 ≤ l› by force
    show ?thesis
      unfolding sol ‹j = 1› pow_list_1
      unfolding pow_pos2[OF ‹0 < l›] rassoc..
  next
    fix r q t
    assume "j = 1" "2 ≤ k" and sol:
      "x =
        ((q ⋅ r) ⋅ (r ⋅ (q ⋅ r) ⇧@ t) ⇧@ (k - 1)) ⇧@ (l - 2) ⋅
        (((q ⋅ r) ⋅ (r ⋅ (q ⋅ r) ⇧@ t) ⇧@ (k - 2)) ⋅ r) ⋅ q"
      "y = r ⋅ (q ⋅ r) ⇧@ t"

    obtain k' where  "Suc (Suc k') = k" using  Suc_minus2[OF ‹2 ≤ k›] by blast

    hence l2: "l - 2 = l'" and l: "l  = l' + 2"  by fastforce+
    show "x ⇧@ j ⋅ y ⇧@ k = z ⇧@ l"

  next
    fix r q t

      "x = (r ⋅ q) ⇧@ t ⋅ r"
      "y = q ⋅ r ⋅ r ⋅ q" "z = (r ⋅ q) ⇧@ t ⋅ r ⋅ r ⋅ q"

Theorem (Addition in Dyadic Algebra):
Given any two elements \(x\) and \(y\) in the dyadic algebra, their sum \(x + y\) also belongs to the dyadic algebra.

lemma dyadics_add:
  assumes "x ∈ dyadics" "y ∈ dyadics"
  shows "x+y ∈ dyadics"
proof -
  obtain i j m n where x: "x = of_nat i / 2 ^ m" and y: "y = of_nat j / 2 ^ n"
    using assms by (auto simp: dyadics_def)
  have xcommon: "x = of_nat(2^n * i) / 2 ^ (m+n)"
    using x by (simp add: power_add)
  moreover
  have ycommon: "y = of_nat(2^m * j) / 2 ^ (m+n)"
    using y by (simp add: power_add)
  ultimately have "x+y = (of_nat(2^n * i + 2^m * j)) / 2 ^ (m+n)"
    by (simp add: field_simps)
  then show ?thesis
    unfolding dyadics_def by blast
qed

Theorem (Multiplication of Natural Numbers):
Given two natural numbers \(a\) and \(b\), their product \(a \times b\) is equal to the sum of their respective unary representations, that is, \(a \times b = \text{of\_nat}(a \cdot b)\).

lemma word_arith_nat_mult: "a * b = of_nat (unat a * unat b)"
  by simp

Theorem (Distributive Property of Scalar Multiplication over Vector Addition):
For any complex vectors \(A, B, C,\) and \(D\), the equality \((A \times B) + (C \times D) = (A + C) \times (B + D)\) holds true.

lemma set_Times_plus_distrib: ‹(A × B) + (C × D) = (A + C) × (B + D)›
  by (auto simp: Sigma_def set_plus_def)

Theorem (Product of Subsets of Natural Numbers):
Given a set of natural numbers \(A\) with a finite number of elements and a subset \(B\) such that \(B \subseteq A\) and \(0\) is not an element of \(B\), the product of all elements in \(A\) divided by the product of all elements in \(B\) is equal to the product of all elements in the set difference \(A - B\). Formally, \(\prod_{a \in A} / \prod_{b \in B} = \prod_{a \in A - B} a\).

lemma prod_id_cancel_nat:
  ― ‹Contributed by Manuel Eberl›
  fixes A::"nat set"
  assumes "B ⊆ A" and "finite A" and "0 ∉ B"
  shows "∏A / ∏B = ∏(A-B)"
  using assms(1-2) by (rule prod_cancel_nat) (metis assms(3))

Theorem (Dot Product of Homogeneous Linear Diophantine Equations):
Given two sequences of integers \(a\) and \(b\) of equal length, the dot product of the sequences \(a\) and \(b\) (denoted as \(a \cdot b\)) is equal to the sum of the products of corresponding elements, that is, \((a \cdot x) \cdot (b \cdot y) = a \cdot b + x \cdot y\).

lemma dotprod_append:
  assumes "length a = length b"
  shows"(a @ x) ∙ (b @ y) = a ∙ b + x ∙ y"
  using assms by (induct a b rule: list_induct2) auto

Theorem (Summation Lemma for Pairwise Sums up to n):
Given non-negative integers \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\), and a natural number \(n\), the sum of products \(a k \cdot b (n - k) \cdot c\) for \(k\) from 0 to \(n\) is equal to the sum of products \(a i \cdot b (s - i) \cdot c\) for \(i\) from 0 to \(s\), where \(s\) ranges from 0 to \(n\).

lemma sum_pair_less_iff:
  "sum (λ((k::nat),m). a k * b m * c (k + m)) {(k,m). k + m ≤ n} =
    sum (λs. sum (λi. a i * b (s - i) * c s) {0..s}) {0..n}"
  (is "?l = ?r")
proof -
  have th0: "{(k, m). k + m ≤ n} = (⋃s∈{0..n}. ⋃i∈{0..s}. {(i, s - i)})"
    by auto
  show "?l = ?r"
    unfolding th0
    by (simp add: sum.UNION_disjoint eq_diff_iff disjoint_iff)
qed

Theorem (Product of Nth Elements in Lists):
Given a set of natural numbers A and a list of natural numbers xs, if B is a subset of A, then the product of the nth elements in xs is equal to the product of the nth elements in B multiplied by the product of the nth elements in the elements of xs that are not in B.
Mathematically, this is expressed as:
\[
\prod_{n \in \text{nths}(xs, A)} x_n = \left(\prod_{n \in \text{nths}(xs, B)}\right) \cdot \left(\prod_{n \in \text{nths}(xs, A \setminus B)}\right)

lemma nths_prod_list_split:
  fixes A :: "nat set" and xs :: "nat list"
  assumes "B ⊆ A"
  shows "prod_list (nths xs A) = (prod_list (nths xs B)) * (prod_list (nths xs (A - B)))"
proof (induction xs rule: rev_induct)
  case Nil
  then show ?case by auto
next
  let ?C = "A - B"
  case (snoc x xs)
  have SA: "nths (xs @ [x]) A = nths xs A @ nths [x] {j. j + length xs ∈ A}" using nths_append[of xs] by auto
  have SB: "nths (xs @ [x]) B = nths xs B @ nths [x] {j. j + length xs ∈ B}" using nths_append[of xs] by auto
  have SC: "nths (xs @ [x]) ?C = nths xs ?C @ nths [x] {j. j + length xs ∈ ?C}" using nths_append[of xs] by auto
  show ?case 
  proof (cases "length xs ∈ A")
    case True
    then have "nths (xs @ [x]) A = nths xs A @ [x]" using SA by auto
    then have eqA: "prod_list (nths (xs @ [x]) A) = prod_list (nths xs A) * x"  by auto
    show ?thesis
    proof (cases "length xs ∈ B")
      case True
      then have "nths (xs @ [x]) B = nths xs B @ [x]" using SB by auto
      then have eqB: "prod_list (nths (xs @ [x]) B) = prod_list (nths xs B) * x"  by auto
      have "length xs ∉ ?C" using True assms by auto
      then have "nths (xs @ [x]) ?C = nths xs ?C" using SC by auto
      then have eqC: "prod_list (nths (xs @ [x]) ?C) = prod_list (nths xs ?C)" by auto
      then show ?thesis using snoc eqA eqB eqC by auto
    next
      case False
      then have "nths (xs @ [x]) B = nths xs B" using SB by auto
      then have eqB: "prod_list (nths (xs @ [x]) B) = prod_list (nths xs B)"  by auto    
      then have "length xs ∈ ?C" using True False assms by auto
      then have "nths (xs @ [x]) ?C = nths xs ?C @ [x]" using SC by auto

    qed
  next
    case False
    then have ninB: "length xs ∉ B" and ninC: "length xs ∉ ?C" using assms by auto

    have "nths (xs @ [x]) A = nths xs A" using SA False nths_singleton by auto
    then have eqA: "prod_list (nths (xs @ [x]) A) = prod_list (nths xs A)" by auto
    have "nths (xs @ [x]) B = nths xs B" using SB ninB nths_singleton by auto
    then have eqB: "prod_list (nths (xs @ [x]) B) = prod_list (nths xs B)" by auto
    have "nths (xs @ [x]) ?C = nths xs ?C" using SC ninC nths_singleton by auto
    then have eqC: "prod_list (nths (xs @ [x]) ?C) = prod_list (nths xs ?C)" by auto
    then show ?thesis using eqA eqB eqC snoc by auto

Theorem (Distributive Law for Intersection over Union):
Given three sets A, B, and C, the intersection of A with the union of B and C is equal to the union of the intersection of A with B and A with C. Formally, \(A \cap (B \cup C) = (A \cap B) \cup (A \cap C)\).

lemma inter_union_distrib_left:
  "A ∩# B + C = (A + C) ∩# (B + C)"
  by (simp add: multiset_eq_iff min_add_distrib_left)

Theorem (Union Size of Multisets):
Given two multisets \(A\) and \(B\), the size of their union is the sum of their individual sizes minus the size of their intersection, expressed as \(\text{size}(A \cup B) = \text{size}(A) + \text{size}(B) - \text{size}(A \cap B)\).

lemma mset_union_size_inter: "size (A ∪# B) = size (A) + size B - size (A ∩# B)"
  by (metis diff_add_inverse2 size_Un_Int)

Theorem (Distributive Property of Intersection over Multiset Union):
Given a set of indices \(I\) and multisets \(A\) and \(B\), the intersection of the multiset formed by the intersection of \(A\) and \(B\) for each index in \(I\) is equal to the intersection of the multisets \(A\) and \(B\) over all indices in \(I\). In mathematical terms, this is expressed as:

\[
\left(\bigcup_{i \in I} (A_i \cap B_i)\right) = \left(\bigcup_{i \in I} A_i\right) \cap \left(\bigcup_{i \in I} B_i\right)
\]

This theorem formalizes the distributive property of intersection over multiset union within the context of nested multisets.

lemma Sigma_mset_Int_distrib2: "(SIGMAMSET i∈#I. A i ∩# B i) = Sigma_mset I A ∩# Sigma_mset I B"
  by (auto simp: multiset_eq_iff count_sum_mset count_image_mset_Pair sum_mset_if_eq_constant
    Sigma_mset_def iterate_op_plus min_def not_in_iff)

Theorem (Sum of Disjoint Sets Distributed Over a Third Set):
Given three sets \(w\), \(x\), and \(y\) that are pairwise disjoint (meaning \(w \cap x = \bot\), \(w \cap y = \bot\), and \(x \cap y = \bot\)), the sum of the intersections of their union with a third set \(z\) is equal to the sum of the individual intersections of \(w\), \(x\), and \(y\) with \(z\). In other words, \(\sum_{z \in (w \cup x \cup y)} ((w \cup x \cup y) \cap z) = \sum_{z \in w} (w \cap z) + \sum_{z \in x} (x \cap z) + \sum_{z \in y} (y \cap z)\).

lemma sum_disjoint_3:
  assumes "w ⊓ x = bot"
      and "w ⊓ y = bot"
      and "x ⊓ y = bot"
    shows "sum ((w ⊔ x ⊔ y) ⊓ z) = sum (w ⊓ z) + sum (x ⊓ z) + sum (y ⊓ z)"
  by (metis assms inf_sup_distrib2 sup_idem sum_disjoint)

Theorem (Distributive Property of Intersection over Multiset Union):
Given two multisets \(I\) and \(J\), the intersection of \(I\) and \(J\) under a certain multiset operation \(C\) distributes over the union of \(I\) and \(J\) in multiset \(C\). Formally, the multiset of the intersection of \(I\) and \(J\) is equal to the intersection of the multisets of \(I\) and \(J\) individually, that is, \(\Sigma_{mset}(I \cap J) C = (\Sigma_{mset} I C) \cap (\Sigma_{mset} J C)\).

lemma Sigma_mset_Int_distrib1: "Sigma_mset (I ∩# J) C = Sigma_mset I C ∩# Sigma_mset J C"
  by (auto simp: multiset_eq_iff count_sum_mset count_image_mset_Pair sum_mset_if_eq_constant
    Sigma_mset_def iterate_op_plus min_def not_in_iff)

Theorem (Union Size of Disjoint Multisets):
Given two disjoint multisets \(A\) and \(B\), the size of their union is the sum of their individual sizes, minus the size of their intersection. Formally, \(\text{size}(A \cup B) = \text{size}(A) + \text{size}(B) - \text{size}(A \cap B)\).

lemma mset_union_size: "size (A ∪# B) = size (A) + size (B - A)"
  by (simp add: union_mset_def)

Theorem (Distributive Law for Intersections over Unions):
For any index sets I and J, the intersection of the unions of sets A indexed by I and B indexed by J is equal to the union of the intersections of A and B indexed by all pairs (i, j) in I × J. Mathematically, this is expressed as \(\bigcup_{i \in I} A_i \cap \bigcup_{j \in J} B_j = \bigcup_{(i, j) \in I \times J} (A_i \cap B_j)\).

lemma Int_UN_distrib2: "(⋃i∈I. A i) ∩ (⋃j∈J. B j) = (⋃i∈I. ⋃j∈J. A i ∩ B j)"
  by blast

Theorem (Distributive Law for Finite Intersection over Union):
For any three sets A, B, and C, the intersection of A with the union of B and C is equal to the union of the intersection of A with B and the intersection of A with C. Mathematically, this is expressed as \(A \cap (B \cup C) = (A \cap B) \cup (A \cap C)\).

lemma finter_funion_distrib: "A |∩| (B |∪| C) = A |∩| B |∪| (A |∩| C)"
  by (rule Int_Un_distrib[Transfer.transferred])

Theorem (Pigeonhole Principle for Intersection of Sets):
Given three finite sets A, B, and C with B and C subsets of A, if the combined size of B and C exceeds the size of A by at most k, then the intersection of B and C has a size that is at most k. Formally, if \(|A| + k \leq |B| + |C|\), then \(|B \cap C| \leq k\).

lemma pigeonhole:
assumes
  finitA: "finite A" and 
  Bss: "B ⊆ A" and Css: "C ⊆ A" and 
  cardH: "card A + k <= card B + card C"
shows "k <= card (B ∩ C)"
proof-
  from Bss Css have "B ∪ C ⊆ A" by blast
  with finitA have "card (B ∪ C) <= card A"
    by (simp add: card_mono)
  with cardH have
      h: "k <= card B + card C - card (B ∪ C)" 
    by arith
  from finitA Bss Css and finite_subset 
  have "finite B ∧ finite C" by auto
  thus ?thesis
    using card_Un_Int and h by force
qed

Theorem (Distributive Property of Intersection over Multiset Product):
For any multisets \(A\), \(B\), and \(C\), the intersection of \(A\) with the product of \(B\) and \(C\) distributes over the product, meaning \((A \cap B) \times C = (A \times C) \cap (B \times C)\).

lemma Times_mset_Int_distrib1: "(A ∩# B) ×# C = A ×# C ∩# B ×# C"
  by (fact Sigma_mset_Int_distrib1)
